2.  While scrutinizing these Orders, the Committee note d that there was a 
considerable time lag between issue  of Notificatio ns and their laying in some cases. 
The annexed statement also indicates the period of delay in cases where 
Notifications have not been laid as per the time sc hedule prescribed by the 
Committee. The Committee observed that out of the t otal 89 delayed Notifications, 
there were 66 Notifications where no delay statement was appended to. However, the 
bulk of delayed Notifications were from the Ministr y of  Road Transport and 
Highways which comes to around 47.1% of the total delayed Notifications. 
 
The observations/recommendations of the Committee i n respect of the 
specific Ministries/Departments where delay in layi ng of Notifications has been 
noticed, are as follows: -  
 

(i) Ministry of  Civil Aviation  
  
 Ministry of Civil Aviation  have laid 3 Notificati ons (Sl. Nos. 23 to 25) out of 
which one Notification ( Sl. No. 25) has been delay ed by 12 months and appended 
delay statement thereto. The reason of delay given by the Ministry is as under:- 
 
 “The Notification to make amendment in rule 2 and t o insert a new sub-rule 
(3) in rule 10A in the Aircraft (Carriage of Danger ous Goods) Rules, 2003 was 
published in the gazette vide G.S.R. No. 275 (E), d ated the 25 
th  February, 2016. The 
authenticated copies of Gazette Notification along with bilingual explanatory notes 
were sent to Lok Sabha/Rajya Sabha Secretariat for laying them on the Table of the 
Houses of Parliament during the Monsoon Session of Parliament 2016. However, 
due to the fact that no business day was left for Ministry of Civil Aviation, the papers  
could not be laid on the Table of the Houses of Par liament. Therefore, Gazette 
Notification is being submitted along with the expl anatory notes before both the 
Houses of Parliament.” 
 
 The reasons cited by Ministry of Civil Aviation  i .e. Notifications could 
not be laid due to the fact that no business day wa s left for Ministry of Civil 
Aviation, is an oft-repeated excuse. It is a statut ory provision to lay the 
Notification within the prescribed time schedule an d the Ministry should have 
taken appropriate action to lay the same in time on  the Table of the House. It 
reflects the lackaidaical approach on the part of t he Ministry. The Committee, 
therefore, impress upon  the Ministry to  devise su itable mechanism to avoid 
such instances of delay in future, particularly, on  account of delay of 
Notifications, so as to adhere to the time schedule  as prescribed in Committee’s 
131 
st  Report.  
 
  
(ii)  Ministry of Commerce and Industry 
 (Department of Commerce)  
 

Ministry of Commerce and Industry (Department of Co mmerce)  have laid  8 
Notifications (Sl. Nos. 26 to 33), out of which 3 N otifications (Sl. Nos. 27 to 29)  
have  been delayed. There is delay of 8 months in e ach case and no delay statement 
appended to any of these delayed Notifications. 
 
The Committee is not happy about the delay in layin g of the three 
Notifications by the Ministry of Commerce and Indus try (Department of 
Commerce) on the Table of the House and also on the ir failure to append the 
delay statement with any of these. The Ministry/Dep artment must ensure that 
Notifications to be laid on the Table of the House in time. It also must ensure to 
append a delay statement in all cases in future. 
 
(iii) Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public  Distribution 
 (Department of Consumer Affairs & Department of Fo od and  Public 
Distribution) 
 
 Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Dist ribution (Department of 
Consumer Affairs) have laid 2 Notifications (Sl. No s. 41 & 42), and both of them 
have been delayed which ranges from 5 to 6 months. There is no delay statement 
appended to both the delayed Notifications. 
Department of  Food and Public Distribution have laid 7 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 43 to 
49), out of which one Notification ( Sl. No. 48) ha s been delayed by 22 months and 
appended delay statement thereto. The reasons of de lay given by the Ministry is as 
under:- 
 
 “Vide letter dated 05.06.2015 this Department had requested Government of 
India Press, Mayapuri to publish the amendment Noti fication in the Gazette of India 
and provide the copy of  printed notification to th is Ministry but the printed 
notification was not received in the Department. Fu rther, on personal visit to the 
Government of India Press, it was informed that the  soft copy of notification is 
available on the website 
www.egazette.nic.in . This Department was unaware that the 
Government of India Press is uploading the Gazette Notifications online nor it was 

informed by the Press despite reminders. Therefore, in the absence of the copy of the 
Gazette Notification No. G.S.R. 469 (e), dated 09.0 6.2015, the same could not be 
laid before the House.” 
 
The Committee does not accept the late receipt of p rinted copies of 
Notifications as a valid reason for delayed laying of Notifications etc. The 
Committee does not accept this as a convincing reas on in respect of laying of 
statutory papers before the Parliament. The Ministr y of Consumer Affairs, 
Food and Public Distribution (Department of Consume r Affairs & Department 
of Food and  Public Distribution)  should, therefor e,  in future ensure that all 
its papers are laid before the House within the tim e frame as prescribed in the 
Committee’s 131 
st  Report. The Ministry should take it up with the Mi nistry of 
Urban Development for late receiving of printed copies of the Notifications. 
 
 
 
(iv) Ministry of Electronics and Information Techno logy  (Department of 
Electronics and Information Technology) 
 
Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology  have laid 2 
Notifications (Sl. No. 75 - 76). One of these Notif ication (Sl. No. 76) has  been 
delayed by 4 months and there is no delay statement appended to it. 
 
 Department of Electronics and Information Technolo gy have laid 3 
Notifications (Sl. Nos. 77 to 79). All of these hav e been delayed by 18 months and 
there is no delay statement to any of these delayed Notifications. 
 
The Committee is constrained to note  that 1 out of  2 Notifications laid 
by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Tech nology, on the Table of the 
House, was delayed and no reasons were given for the same.  
Similarly, the Department of Electronics and Inform ation Technology 
have laid 3 Notifications and all of them were delayed by 18 Months and none of 

them had a delay statement appended to it.  As a re sult, Committee is not aware 
of the reason for this delay. The Committee view th is very seriously and feels 
that not appending the delay statements is akin to infringement of Parliament’s 
right to know the facts of the case. Hence, the Com mittee reiterates  its 
recommendations, as contained in its 131 st  and 135 th  Reports, emphasizing 
timely laying of  Notifications  on the Table of th e House and appending a delay 
statement wherever there has been a delay.  
 
(v) Ministry of External Affairs 
 
The Ministry of External Affairs has laid only one notification (Sl. No. 80) 
and that was also delayed by 9 months. Further, the re was also no delay statement 
appended to it. 
     
 The Committee is concerned with the inordinate dela y in laying of the 
notification, which was around 9 months. Further no  delay statement was also 
appended as a result the Committee is not aware of the reason for  this delay. 
The Committee therefore, impresses upon the Ministr y to take care that such 
instances of delay do not recur in future and in ca se of  such delay is 
unavoidable, then a delay statement should invariab ly be appended to the 
Notification at the time of laying.  
 
  
(vi) Ministry of Finance 
  (Department of Revenue) 
 
 During the session the Ministry of Finance (Depart ment of Revenue) have 
laid 124 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 130 to 253). Out o f  these 20 Notifications have been 
delayed. The delay period ranges from 4 months to 1 9 months. Ten  Notifications 
(Sl. nos.182 – 189 and 192 – 193) have delay statem ent appended to them. Another 
10 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 139 –144, 172, 181  and 190 – 191) have not attached any 

delay statement. The reasons cited by Ministry that inadvertently delayed by the Cus-
IV Section. Notifications could not be laid on the Table of the House on time. 
 
 The Committee appreciates the hard work put in by the Ministry of 
Finance (Department of Revenue) in laying of fairly  large number of 
Notifications on the Table of the House in time and  keeping the delay in laying 
the Notifications to the minimum.  However, the Com mittee takes strong 
exception to the Ministry’s failure to lay the delay statement. The Committee, in 
the absence of delay statements, are not able to kn ow the reasons behind this 
delay. Therefore, the Committee invites attention t o its recommendation 
contained in its 135 
th  Report  in this connection wherein it has been emp hasized 
to append invariably a delay statement in case of d elay in laying of notifications 
by  the Ministry. The Ministry of Finance (Departme nt of Revenue) should also 
endeavour to avoid recurrence of such delays in future. 
 The Committee does not accept the reply forwarded by the Ministry of 
Finance (Department of Revenue)  that the Notificat ions could not be laid on 
time due to inadvertence in putting up by the secti on concerned. It only reflects 
the lack of seriousness on the part of the Ministry  in fulfilling its constitutional 
responsibility to Parliament. The Committee expects  the Ministry to be more 
careful about laying of its papers and see that per sons responsible for this are 
held accountable so that there are no such recurrences. 
  
  
(vii)  Ministry of Health and Family Welfare & (Dep artment of Health and 
Family Welfare) 
 
 Ministry of Health and Family Welfare have laid 4 N otifications (Sl. Nos. 
254 to 257), out of which 2 Notifications have been  delayed which ranges from 6 to 
22 months. One Notification (Sl. No. 254) has delay  statement attached to it and 
another one Notification has no delay statement app ended to them. The reasons for 
delay given by the Ministry is that due to oversight Notifications could not be laid on 
the Table of the House:- 

  
 The Committee cannot consider the reasons given by  the Ministry of 
Health and Family Welfare as convincing that Notifi cations could not be laid on 
the Table of the House due to oversight. This is sh eer lackadaisical approach on 
the part of the Ministry to have neglected their co nstitutional responsibility. 
This approach calls for relook/introspection so as to bring improvement in the 
current situation.  
 
 Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (Department of Health and Family 
Welfare) have laid 13 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 258 t o 270). Out of these one 
Notification (Sl. No. 267) is delayed by 6 months a nd no  delay statement  attached  
thereto. 
  
 The Committee notes that there has been delay in l aying of one 
Notification and no delay statement has been attach ed to it. The Committee 
reiterates its recommendation contained in its 135 
th  Report that in case of delay 
in laying of Notifications etc., invariably, a dela y statement should be attached. 
The Ministry/Department should ensure such compliance in future. 
 
 
(viii) Ministry of Human Resource Development 
 (Department of Higher Education) 
  
Ministry of Human Resource Development (Department of Higher 
Education)  have laid 17 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 288 to 304). O ut of  these,  9  
Notifications have been delayed  huge time period  for 5 months to 5 years and 9 
months. There is no delay statement appended to 5 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 288 – 290, 
292 & 295). Other 4 delayed Notifications (Sl. No. 291, 293 – 294 and 296) have 
appended with delay statement. The reasons for dela y  given by the Ministry is  as 
under:- 
 

“As per the provisions of Rule 43 of Central Univer sity Act, 2009, every 
Statute, Ordinances or Regulation made under the Ac t, shall be laid as soon as may 
be after it is made, before each House of Parliamen t, while it is in session, for a total 
period of thirty days which may be comprised in one  session or in two or more 
successive sessions, and if, before the expiry of t he session immediately following 
the session or the successive sessions. 
The Ministry received these Gazette Notifications i n the last week of 
December, 2016 only. Therefore, it could not be laid in the Parliament earlier and the 
same is now being laid.” 
 
Although 50% of the total Notifications are delayed , yet the Committee 
is to see that statutory obligation of laying the N otifications on the Table of 
House as prescribed by it is fulfilled by the Minis tries. It is for the Ministries to 
see that this job is performed by them without flaw  but Ministry of Human 
Resource Development (Department of Higher Educatio n) have failure on this 
count. Therefore, Committee urges upon the Ministry  of Human Resource 
Development (Department of Higher Education) to see to it that hurdles causing 
delay in laying of Notifications, such as conclusion of Parliament Session, should 
have been handled beforehand or preparations for la ying should have been 
made earlier so that the situation could have been avoided. 
The Committee are surprised at the length of time t aken by the Ministry 
of Human Resource Development (Department of Higher  Education) in laying 
of their Notifications extending from five months t o almost six years!  The 
Committee is unable to accept the reasons given by the Ministry for the delay in 
laying, such as, late receiving of printed copies o f Notifications. It only reflects 
the lack of seriousness in the Ministry in fulfilli ng its constitutional 
responsibility towards  Parliament. The Committee e xpects the Ministry to be 
careful about laying of its papers and see to it th at persons responsible for this 
important obligation remain vigilant about it.  
 
 
(ix) Ministry of Information and Broadcasting 

 
 The Ministry of  Information and Broadcasting have  laid 4 Notifications (Sl. 
Nos. 305 – 308). Out of these,  2 Notifications (Sl . Nos. 305 and 308) have been 
delayed. The delay period ranges from 5 months to 7  months. Both of  delayed 
Notifications are accompanied by delay statement. T he Ministry have cited 
administrative reasons for not laying the Notifications in time. 
 
 The Committee hopes that the Ministry of Informati on and Broadcasting 
would avoid such instances of delay in laying of subordinate legislation in future 
and would remove lacuna, if any, administrative or otherwise, causing delay. 
The Committee also impresses upon the Ministry to t ake note of the fact that in 
case there is a delay in the laying of any Statutor y Notification, the same should 
be accompanied by a delay statement while it is bei ng laid . The Committee also 
advises the Ministry to avoid recurrence of delays due to administrative 
reasons. 
 
(x) Ministry of  Labour and Employment 
 
 The Ministry of Labour and Employment have laid 19  Notifications (Sl. Nos. 
309 – 327) and one of these have been delayed by 10  months. There is no delay 
statement appended with the Notification. 
  
 The Committee is unhappy over the delay in laying o f one of its 
Notification on the Table of the House. The Committ ee desires the Ministry of 
Labour and Employment to strictly adhere to the tim e schedule in laying of 
Notifications. The Committee further stresses that the Ministry of Labour and 
Employment should append a delay statement where th ere is delay in laying of 
Notification on the Table of the House. 
 
(xi) Ministry of Road Transport and Highways 
 

 The Ministry of Road Transport & Highways have lai d 99 Notifications  on 
the Table of the House (Sl. Nos. 361 to 459). A tot al of 42 Notifications have been 
delayed out of which 4 Notifications are accompanie d by delay statements and 38 
Notifications have no delay statements appended with them. The delay period ranges 
from 7 months to 27 months. The reasons given by th e Ministry is that it took some 
time to complete the procedural formalities and, therefore, papers could not be laid in 
time. 
 
 The Committee takes note of the fact that Ministry  of Road Transport 
and Highways have to lay  huge volume of Notificati ons on the table of the 
House.  The Committee, however, finds that percenta ge of delayed Notifications 
out of total Notifications laid is quite high i.e. as high as over 42%. This is 
simply unacceptable. Further, Ministry have not app ended any delay statement 
with many delayed Notifications/Rules. Ministry of Road Transport and 
Highways should see or look into the matter seriously to eliminate recurrence of 
such delays in completing the procedural formalitie s. The Committee desires 
that Ministry of Road Transport and Highways should  adhere to the time 
schedule in laying of Notifications as prescribed i n Committee’s 131 st  Report 
and append a delay statement in case there is  dela y in laying. This has, sort of 
become a matter of routine with this Ministry, its seems. The Ministry may 
clarify the reasons for delay in laying and also wh y the delay statement has not 
been appended to the Notifications. 
 
 
 3.   The Committee impresses upon all the Ministrie s/Departments to take 
immediate and concrete steps to ensure timely and p roper laying of subordinate 
legislation. The Committee, accordingly, wishes to bring to the notice of all 
Ministries/Departments of the Government of India, particularly, the defaulting ones, 
the following recommendations, as contained in its 7 
th , 10 th , 131 
st 
, 135 
th 
, 152 
nd ,  
192 nd  , 201 st , 212 th  and 213 th  Reports: 
 

 “The Committee desires that for the convenience of  the public and 
Members, Ministries should henceforth send copies o f 'order' duly 
authenticated by the Ministers concerned, incorpora ting therein all the 
corrections and amendments issued till date of layi ng such 'orders' instead of 
laying the uncorrected copy along with corrigenda. The Committee feels that to 
obviate any legal or technical difficulty, Ministri es should examine whether 
there is any necessity of assigning a separate G.S. R. No. to a corrigendum at the 
time of its publication in the Gazette and whether such a corrigendum should 
not be published without assigning any G.S.R. No. T he Committee would, 
therefore, like to impress upon all Ministries of t he Government of India that 
the present practice of laying the rules without in corporating corrigenda in the 
body of the rules is not a healthy one. The Committ ee hopes that the Ministries 
will ensure supply of only corrected copies of the rules for laying on the Table so 
that they depict a true and correct picture and serve the desired purpose."  
(7 th   Report) 
(Presented on 12 th   May, 1969) 
 
 The Committee approve the following draft revised formula for laying of 
Statutory Rules before both Houses of Parliament wh ich the Ministry of Law 
and Justice propose to incorporate in all future le gislation which provide for 
making of rules by the CentralGovernment:— 
 
 "Every rule made by the Central Government under t his Act shall be laid, 
as soon as may be after it is made, before each Hou se of Parliament, while 
it is in session, for a total period of thirty days  which may be comprised in 
one session or in two or more successive sessions, and if, before the expiry 
of the session immediately following the session or  the successive sessions 
aforesaid, both Houses agree in making any modifica tion in the rule or 
both Houses agree that the rule should not be made,  the rule shall 
thereafter have effect only in such modified form o r be of no effect, as the 
case may be; so, however that any such modification  or annulment shall be 

without prejudice to the validity of anything previ ously done under that 
rule." 
  
The Committee recommend that the revised formula sh ould be incorporated 
not only in new legislation but also in the existin g Acts as and when Bills to 
amend them are brought before Parliament. The Minis try should also 
incorporate the new formula in the Bills pending be fore Parliament. This will, 
in the opinion of the Committee, bring about unifor mity in the matter 
expeditiously. 
 
(10 
th   Report) 
(presented on 24 th  May, 1971) 
 
 
 “Orders required to be laid before the House shoul d be laid (i) if the House 
is not in Session, during the Session immediately f ollowing the date of 
publication of the Order in the Official Gazette an d (ii) if the House is in 
Session, on the date of the publication of the Orde r, during its continuance and 
in case the time lag between the date of publication and the date of the closing of 
the Session is less than 15 clear days, before the expiry of the Session 
immediately following the said Session. All the Min istries/Departments of 
Government of India should henceforth comply with t his schedule in the matter 
of laying of the Orders issued under various Acts o f Parliament on the Table of 
the Rajya Sabha. 
 
(131 st  Report) 
(Presented on 15 
th   December 2000) 
 
 
 
 “The Committee has, time and again, emphasized tha t it is essential that in 
case there is a delay in the laying of Statutory Or ders, the concerned 

Ministry/Department should invariably append a dela y statement along with 
the Notifications being laid so as to apprise Parli ament of the causes of delay. 
The Committee desires all Ministries/Departments to  take a note of this, since 
the intention is that through the process of formulation of a delay statement, the 
Ministry is able to introspect, identify bottleneck s and devise remedial 
measures”. 
(135 th  Report) 
(Presented on 27 th   July 2001) 
 
 “In the opinion of the Committee, every notificati on should be assigned a 
distinctive number in order to give it a separate i dentity and similarly, no 
notification should be published/laid which does no t carry a notification 
number. The Committee expects all Ministries/Depart ments of Government of 
India to exercise caution in this regard. In case w here there are more than one 
Notifications under a single file, the Ministries/D epartments should ensure that 
the file number on each notification should be suit ably distinguished from one 
another.” 
(152 
nd 
 Report) 
(Presented on 26 th   August 2004)  
 
 “In addition to the concern expressed by the Commi ttee over delay in 
laying of Notifications on the Table of the House, the Committee also express 
their deep concern over delay in framing of rules/r egulations under different 
Acts. The Committee in its 47 
th  report presented to the House on 14.9.1981 has 
recommended that the rule-making process should be completed within a 
period of six months of the coming into force of an  Act. The Committee has 
further recommended that in case a Ministry is not able to adhere to this time 
limit, it should seek extension of time for complet ing the rule-making process. 
The recommendation of the committee reads as follows:- 
 

  “The Committee feels that the rule-making process c ould well 
have been completed within the time limit of six mo nths which the 
Committee has laid down for making of rules under a n Act after coming 
into force of that Act. Where however, a Ministry d oes not find it possible 
to adhere to the time limit, they should inform the  Committee of the 
reasons why they cannot make rules within the time limit and seek 
extension of time for completing the rule-making process.” 
  
 The Committee is constrained to take note of the f act that the 
Ministries/Departments of Government of India are n ot complying with the 
Committee’s recommendation to complete the process of framing of 
subordinate legislation contemplated under various Acts of Parliament within a 
period of six months. At the same time, the Committ ee also does not receive 
requests for extension of time for completing the r ule-making process in terms 
of its recommendations as above from most of the Mi nistries/Departments. The 
Committee takes a serious note of the prevailing si tuation in which the 
Ministries/Departments are neither able to complete  the task of framing 
rules/regulations under different Acts within the g iven six months’ period nor 
do they suo-motu  approach the Committee for seeking extension of ti me. The 
Committee further notes that in order to ensure tim ely framing of 
rules/regulations it has taken an initiative to mon itor the progress of framing of 
subordinate legislation in respect of all legislati ons brought about by different 
Ministries/Departments of Government of India from the year 2003 onwards 
with a view to ensure that the framing of subordina te legislation is not delayed. 
The Committee, however, finds that the responses fr om the 
Ministries/Departments have not been prompt in this  monitoring exercise 
undertaken on behalf of the Committee. 
  
 In view of the above position, the Committee once again reiterates its 
recommendation that the Ministries/Departments shou ld ensure putting in 
place subordinate legislation positively within a p eriod of six months of coming 

into force of the Act. The Committee further recomm ends that in case the 
Ministry fails to meet with this deadline, they sho uld invariably approach the 
Committee for seeking extension of time. The Commit tee further recommends 
that in cases where the time limit of six months is  not adhered to, they should, 
while laying rules/regulations before the Parliamen t invariably lay a statement 
explaining the reasons why the framing of rules/regulations was delayed beyond 
six months so as to keep the Parliament apprised of  the compliance of the 
Parliament’s mandate  conferred upon the Executive.” 
(192 
nd 
 Report) 
(Presented on 26 th   August 2011)  
 
  Rules/Regulations/Orders/bye-laws are laid by dif ferent Ministries on 
the Table of the House under various provisions of parent Acts passed by 
Parliament. These Rules/ Regulations/Orders/bye-law s are published in the 
official Gazette before being laid on the Table of the House. Even after they are 
laid, it is very difficult to get access to these N otifications. The Committee 
recommends that such Rules/Regulations/Orders, etc.  laid on the Table of the 
House should be invariably uploaded on the websites  of respective Ministries 
immediately on the same day when they have been lai d on the Table of the 
House, for information of Members of Parliament and  people at large for their 
easy access. 
201 
st  Report 
(Presented on 14 th  December, 2012)  
 
The Committee observes that the whole process of en acting laws is 
defeated if rules are not framed and laid on the Ta ble of the House in time.  A 
reasonable delay could be understood but unjustifia bly long delays should be 
avoided and the Ministries should work towards impr oving this position.   The 
Committee hopes that Ministry would strive to keep the delay to the minimum 
and take care that Notifications are laid on the Ta ble of the House at the first 
available opportunity after publication of Notifications. 
 

The Committee would like to impress upon the Minist ry that it is their 
responsibility to ensure that copies of the Notific ations are printed timely and 
for this purpose, they need to evolve a suitable me chanism to ensure that 
notifications are laid in time.   The Committee is happy that the Ministry has 
evolved an internal mechanism/ procedure for this p urpose.  The Committee 
hopes that it would take action accordingly in orde r to comply with the 
prescribed schedule in the matter of laying of statutory Notifications. 
 
The Ministry must take appropriate step to remove l acuna, if any, 
administrative or otherwise, causing such long dela y by being little proactive 
and prompt.  Further, the Ministries should take it  up with the Ministry of 
Urban Development for late receiving of printed copies of the Notification. 
212 
th   Report 
(Presented on  3 rd  September, 2013) 
 
 “The Committee is not inclined to accept the late availability of printed 
copies of Notifications from the Government of Indi a Press as the reason for 
delay in laying of the Notifications. The Committee  directs all the Ministries 
that in case there is a delay in procuring printed copies in time, they may obtain 
G.S.R. and S.O. numbers from the Government of Indi a Press and prepare 
requisite number of copies in cyclostyled form for laying in the Parliament. The 
Committee also recommends that this process may be adopted by Ministries suo 
moto  on immediate basis so as to avoid such delays henceforth”. 
213 
th   Report 
(Presented on  19 th  February, 2014)

statement appended to the Notification.

by the Ministry of Civil Aviation in laying of one of the 
Notification on the Table of the House. The Committ ee 
desires the Ministry should  have communicated the 
circumstances causing the delay in laying of Notifi cation. 
However, the Committee finds that the Ministry have  not 
only delayed the laying of one Notification but also did not 
append any delay statement thereto. The Committee, 
therefore, advises the Ministry to strictly adhere to the 
time schedule in laying of the Notifications and ap pend a 
delay statement whenever there is delay in laying o f 
Notification on the Table of the House.  
 
 
(ii) Ministry of Communications 
 (Department of Telecommunications) 
 
The Ministry of Communications (Department of 
Telecommunications) have laid 14 Notifications (Sl.  Nos. 27 
to 40). Out of these, 3 Notifications have been del ayed. The 
delay period ranges from 7 months to 14 months, app ended 
with delay statement to all of these delayed Notifications. The 

reasons given by the Ministry for the said delay is  reproduced 
as under:-  
 
 “English and Hindi version of the TRAI Regulation 
No. 7/2016 – The Mobile Banking (Quality of Service ) (2 
nd  
Amendment) Regulations, 2016 were notified on 22.11 .2016 
and 23.11.2016 respectively. The above Notification s were 
forwarded to Rajya Sabha on 23.03.2017 for laying t he same 
on the Table of Rajya Sabha. The Rajya Sabha Secret ariat 
returned the notifications saying that the date of the 
Regulation in English and Hindi versions are differ ent. Rajya 
Sabha Secretariat gave direction that if the Depart ment wants 
to lay the regulation on the Table of the Rajya Sab ha, a 
Corrigendum is required to be issued which should b e laid on 
the Table of the House. 
 Accordingly, a Corrigendum to above Regulations 
was notified by TRAI on 30.03.2017 and the same was  
received in the Department on 07.04.2017 i.e. the l ast date of 
Session of Rajya Sabha. Hence, due to paucity of ti me and 
administrative reasons, the TRAI Regulations No. 7/ 2016 
same could not be laid timely on the Table of the R ajya 
Sabha.” 
 “The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) 
Regulations No. 4/2016 – The Telecom Regulatory Aut hority 
of India (Officers and Staff Appointment) (Eleventh  
Amendment) Regulation, 2016 dated 08.06.2016 was no t in 
line with the existing Rules. Upon the clarificatio ns obtained 
from the TRAI as reflected in the Regulation No. 03 /2017- 
The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (Officers  and 
Staff Appointment) (Twelfth Amendment) Regulation, 2017 
dated 27/07/2017, it has now been decided to lay bo th the 
Regulations in the House.” 
 

 The Committee noted with serious concern that the 
Ministry of Communications (Department of 
Telecommunications) have failed to lay the Notifica tions 
in time on the Table of the House. The laying of 
Notifications on the Table of the House is a statut ory 
obligation which should be fulfilled without delay.  
However, the Ministry have shown lukewarm approach 
towards their duty to the Parliament. They should 
manage the time schedule properly. The Committee, 
therefore,  recommends that the Ministry of 
Communications (Department of Telecommunications) 
should adhere strictly to the schedule as recommend ed by 
the Committee in its 131 
st  Report for timely laying of the 
Subordinate Legislation.  
 
  
 
 
(iii) Ministry of Electronics and Information 
Technology 
  
The Ministry of Electronics and Information 
Technology have laid only one  Notification (Sl. No s. 78) 
during the Session which has been delayed by 8 mont hs and 
moreover no delay statement has been appended to it.  
 
The Committee reiterates its recommendations 
made in its 135 
th  Report, that it is essential to append a 
delay statement in case of delay in laying of statu tory 
orders. The Committee, therefore, impresses upon th e 
Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology to 
strictly adhere to the time schedule in laying of 
Notifications and should append delay statement in case 
of any delay . 

 
 
(iv) Ministry of Finance 
 (Department of Economic Affairs)  
 
The Ministry of Finance (Department of Economic 
Affairs) have laid 48 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 83 to  130) and a 
large number of these Notifications have been delayed i.e.  26 
delayed Notifications (Sl. Nos. 84, 87 – 88, 98, 10 0, 103 – 
105, 110 &  113 – 129) and  none of them have been attached 
with delay statement. The delay period ranges from 4 months 
to 27 months and in 7 cases, Notifications have bee n delayed 
by a period ranging from 24 months to  27 months.  
 
The Committee is not happy over such a large 
number of delayed Notifications. This is just not 
acceptable to the Committee that 26 out of 48 
Notifications which were delayed, did not even have  the 
mandatory delay statements. Further, the , delay pe riods 
were more than one year in majority  of Notificatio ns laid 
and 5 Notifications were delayed by more than 24 mo nths. 
While there may be a reason for the delay, but ther e 
cannot be any reason for not furnishing reasons for  the 
same. The Ministry must understand the implications  for 
not doing so and in such a large number of cases wh ich 
put the Ministry in poor light. The Committee also 
reiterates earlier recommendations made in its 135 
th  
Report, wherein it is laid down that it is essentia l to 
append a delay statement in case of delay in laying  of 
statutory orders. The Committee, therefore, impress es 
upon the Ministry of Finance (Department of Economi c 
Affairs) to strictly adhere to the time schedule in  laying of 
Notifications and to invariably append delay statem ent in 
each case of  delayed Notifications . The Committee 

recommends that the Ministry may clarify the reason s for 
the delay and also why the delay statement has not been 
appended to the Notification. 
 
 
 
 
(v) Ministry of  Health and Family Welfare 
 (Department of Health and Family Welfare) 
  
 
The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare 
(Department of Health and Family Welfare) have laid  8 
Notifications (Sl. Nos. Sl. Nos. 412 to 419) during  the 
Session. Out of these, 4 (50%) Notifications have b een 
delayed  by 5 months to  8  months and moreover no delay 
statement were  appended to any of them.  
 
 The Committee expresses its unhappiness over the 
large proportion of Notifications delayed by the Mi nistry 
which comes to around 50% of the total Notifications. The 
Committee further takes serious note of the fact th at the 
Ministry even did not bother to provide the reasons  for 
such delayed laying of Notifications. In absence of  any 
delay statement with any of the delayed Notificatio ns, the 
Ministry/Department must realise the possible 
implications of failing to meet this requirement th at 
tantamounts to diluting Executive’s accountability to the 
Parliament. It must ensure to append a delay statem ent in 
all such cases in future. 
 
  
 
(vi) Ministry of  Home Affairs  

 
The Ministry of Home Affairs have laid 61 
Notifications (Sl. Nos. 420 to 480)  Out of these 6   
Notifications (Sl. Nos. 421 – 423, 449 – 450  & 456 ) have 
been  delayed by a period ranging from 5 months to 1 year. 
There is no delay statement appended to any of thes e delayed 
Notifications. 
 
 The Committee takes a serious note of the fact tha t 
Ministry of Home Affairs  have laid 6 Notifications 
without delay statements where delay has been inordinate. 
This reflects their negligence of Parliamentary pra ctices 
and procedures.  Delay period of more than 1 year 
without  a delay statement, is a reflection on the 
functioning of the Ministry of Home Affairs. The Ministry 
should, therefore,  look into the matter seriously to 
eliminate recurrence of such delays in future.

(viii)  Ministry of Law and Justice 
 (Department of Justice) 
  
The Ministry of Law and Justice (Department of 
Justice)  have laid 3 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 544 t o 546). Two 
of them (Sl. Nos. 544 and 545) have been delayed. T he delay 
period ranges from 24 months to  30 months and are 
accompanied with delay statement to both the delaye d 
Notifications. The reason given by the Ministry for delay is as 
under:-  
 
“The National Legal Services Authority Rules, 1995 
has been amended by way of Notification G.S.R. 75 ( E), 
dated 05.02.2015. The National Legal Services Autho rities 
(Amendment) Rules, 2016 and the National Legal Serv ices 
Authority Rules, 1995 has been amended by way of 
Notification  No. S.O. 2164 (E), dated 12.08.2015. The 
National Legal Services Authorities (Second Amendme nt) 
Rules, 2015 could not be laid before the House of t he 
Parliament, due to administrative reasons.” 
 
The Committee does not accept the reasons of 
delay given by the Ministry of Law and Justice 
(Department of Justice) and expresses its serious c oncern 
over such inordinate delays which ranges from 24 mo nths 
to 30 months. The Committee wonders  how 
administrative procedural process can take 24 to 30  

months to receive Notifications and complete proced ural 
formalities. The Committee feels that Ministry did not 
take adequate precaution to avoid the delay and mad e no 
serious efforts to lay the Notifications in time wh ich is in 
contravention of its statutory obligation to Parlia ment. 
The Committee recommends that the Ministry must tak e 
appropriate steps to remove the lacuna, if any, due  to 
administrative or any other reason causing such lon g 
delay and wish it  would strive to keep delay to th e 
minimum by playing a more proactive role and pursui ng 
with the concerned organisations to act with prompt ness 
in future. 
 
 
(ix) Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas 
 
 The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas have lai d 
3 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 560 to 562). Only 1 Notif ication (Sl. 
No. 560) has been delayed by 5 months and there is no delay 
statement appended to it.  
  
   The Committee is not happy to see that 1 out of 3 
Notifications that the Ministry of Petroleum and Na tural 
Gas have laid, has been delayed and no reason has b een 
given for this delay.  This is in contravention of 
Committee’s recommendation given in its 135 
th   Report 
that Notifications, which are delayed, should invariably be 
accompanied by a delay statement. The Committee wou ld 
like the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas to t ake 
necessary steps to obviate such delays and in case of delay 
in laying of Notifications, delay statements should  
invariably be appended to them. 
  
 

 
(x) Ministry of Road Transport and Highways 
 
 The Ministry of Road Transport & Highways have 
laid 56 Notifications
 on the Table of the House (Sl. Nos. 569 
to 624). A total of  7 Notifications have been dela yed out of 
which 2 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 569 – 570)  are accompanied 
by delay statements and 5 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 5 81 –585)  
have no delay statements appended with them. The de lay 
period ranges from 4 months to 5 months. The reason s given 
by the Ministry is that it took some time to comple te the 
procedural formalities and, therefore, papers could  not be laid 
in time. 
 
The Committee does not accept the reasons of the 
delay given by the Ministry of Road Transport and 
Highways that it took some time to collect the pape rs and 
complete the procedural formalities. The Committee 
wonders how can it take five months to receive 
Notifications and to complete procedural formalitie s. The 
Committee feels that Ministry did not take adequate  
precaution to avoid the delay. The Committee furthe r 
takes a serious view of the fact that even after delay of five 
months in two case Ministry did not feel it necessa ry to 
append a delay statement so as to apprise the Parli ament 
of the reasons for the delay. The Committee recomme nds 
that the Ministry should initiate urgent measures s o as to 
avoid delay in completing the procedural formalitie s so 
that such delay can be eliminated. 
 
 
 
 
(xi)  Ministry of Textiles 

 
 The Ministry of Textiles have laid 2 Notifications  
during the Session (Sl. Nos. 638 to 639). There is only one 
Notification (Sl. No. 538) which was delay by a per iod of 26 
months and a delay statement has been appended ther eto. The 
reasons given by the Ministry are as follows:- 
 
 “The requirement of laying of the Central Silk Boa rd 
(Administrative, Accounts and General Cadre Posts) 
Recruitment Rules, 2015 and corrigendum thereon pub lished 
in Part II – Section 3 – Sub-Section (i) of the Gaz ette of 
Indian Extraordinary Notification dated 11.12.2015 and 
03.06.2016 before the House could not be complied w ith due 
to lack of clarity whether it should be laid in the  House of 
Parliament or otherwise as per Department of Person nel & 
Training’s O.M. No. 14017/48/2010-Estt. (RR) dated 
31.12.2010, hence the delay is regretted.” 
  
 The Committee does not appreciate the reasons 
given by the Ministry of Textiles that Notification s could 
not be laid on the Table of the House due to lack o f 
clarity. This is sheer lackadaisical approach on th e part of 
the Ministry to have neglected the constitutional 
responsibility. This approach calls for 
relook/introspection so as to bring improvement in the 
current situation. 
 The Committee hopes that the Ministry of Textiles 
would avoid such instances of delay in laying of 
subordinate legislation in future and would remove 
lacuna, if any, causing delay. The Committee also a dvises 
the Ministry to avoid recurrence of such delays in future.  
 
3.   The Committee impresses upon all the 
Ministries/Departments to take immediate steps to e nsure 

timely and proper laying of subordinate legislation . The 
Committee, accordingly, wishes to bring to the noti ce of all 
Ministries/Departments of the Government of India, 
particularly, the defaulting ones, the following 
recommendations, as contained in its 131 
st 
, 135 
th 
, 152 
nd 
,   
192 nd ,  201 st ,  212 th  and 213 th  Reports: 
 
 “Orders required to be laid before the House shoul d 
be laid (i) if the House is not in Session, during the Session 
immediately following the date of publication of the Order 
in the Official Gazette and (ii) if the House is in  Session, 
on the date of the publication of the Order, during  its 
continuance and in case the time lag between the da te of 
publication and the date of the closing of the Sess ion is 
less than 15 clear days, before the expiry of the S ession 
immediately following the said Session. All the 
Ministries/Departments of Government of India shoul d 
henceforth comply with this schedule in the matter of 
laying of the Orders issued under various Acts of 
Parliament on the Table of the Rajya Sabha. 
(131 st  Report) 
(Presented on 15 December 2000) 
 
 “The Committee has, time and again, emphasized 
that it is essential that in case there is a delay in the laying 
of Statutory Orders, the concerned Ministry/Departm ent 
should invariably append a delay statement along with the 
Notifications being laid so as to apprise Parliamen t of the 
causes of delay. The Committee desires all 
Ministries/Departments to take a note of this, sinc e the 
intention is that through the process of formulatio n of a 
delay statement, the Ministry is able to introspect, identify 
bottlenecks and devise remedial measures”. 

(135 th  Report) 
(Presented on 27 July 2001) 
 
 “In the opinion of the Committee, every notificati on 
should be assigned a distinctive number in order to  give it 
a separate identity and similarly, no notification should be 
published/laid which does not carry a notification 
number. The Committee expects all 
Ministries/Departments of Government of India to 
exercise caution in this regard. In case where ther e are 
more than one Notifications under a single file, th e 
Ministries/Departments should ensure that the file 
number on each notification should be suitably 
distinguished from one another.” 
(152 
nd 
 Report) 
(Presented on 26 August 2004)  
 
 “In addition to the concern expressed by the 
Committee over delay in laying of Notifications on the 
Table of the House, the Committee also express thei r deep 
concern over delay in framing of rules/regulations under 
different Acts. The Committee in its 47 
th  report presented 
to the House on 14.9.1981 has recommended that the rule-
making process should be completed within a period of six 
months of the coming into force on an Act. The 
Committee has further recommended that in case a 
Ministry is not able to adhere to this time limit, it should 
seek extension of time for completing the rule-maki ng 
process. The recommendation of the committee reads as 
follows:- 
 

  “The Committee feels that the rule-
making process could well have been completed 
within the time limit of six months which the 
Committee has laid down for making of rules 
under an Act after coming into force of that Act. 
Where however, a Ministry does not find it possible 
to adhere to the time limit, they should inform the  
Committee of the reasons why they cannot make 
rules within the time limit and seek extension of 
time for completing the rule-making process.” 
 The Committee is constrained to take note of the 
fact that the Ministries/Departments of Government of 
India are not complying with the Committee’s 
recommendation to complete the process of framing o f 
subordinate legislation contemplated under various Acts 
of Parliament within a period of six months. At the  same 
time, the Committee also does not receive requests for 
extension of time for completing the rule-making pr ocess 
in terms of its recommendations as above from most of 
the Ministries/Departments. The Committee takes a 
serious note of the prevailing situation in which t he 
Ministries/Departments are neither able to complete  the 
task of framing rules/regulations under different A cts 
within the given six months’ period nor do they suo-motu  
approach the Committee for seeking extension of tim e. 
The Committee further notes that in order to ensure  
timely framing of rules/regulations it has taken an  
initiative to monitor the progress of framing of 
subordinate legislation in respect of all legislati ons 
brought about by different Ministries/Departments o f 
Government of India from the year 2003 onwards with  a 
view to ensure that the framing of subordinate legi slation 
is not delayed. The Committee, however, finds that the 

responses from the Ministries/Departments have not been 
prompt in this monitoring exercise undertaken on be half 
of the Committee. 
  
 In view of the above position, the Committee once 
again reiterates its recommendation that the 
Ministries/Departments should ensure putting in pla ce 
subordinate legislation positively within a period of six 
months of coming into force of the Act. The Committ ee 
further recommends that in case the Ministry fails to meet 
with this deadline, they should invariably approach  the 
Committee for seeking extension of time. The Commit tee 
further recommends that in cases where the time lim it of 
six months is not adhered to, they should, while la ying 
rules/regulations before the Parliament invariably lay a 
statement explaining the reasons why the framing of  
rules/regulations was delayed beyond six months so as to 
keep the Parliament apprised of the compliance of t he 
Parliament’s mandate  conferred upon the Executive.” 
(192 
nd 
 Report) 
(Presented on 26 August 2011)  
 
  “Rules/Regulations/Orders/bye-laws are laid by 
different Ministries on the Table of the House unde r 
various provisions of parent Acts passed by Parliam ent. 
These Rules/ Regulations/Orders/bye-laws are publis hed 
in the official Gazette before being laid on the Table of the 
House. Even after they are laid, it is very difficu lt to get 
access to these Notifications. The Committee recomm ends 
that such Rules/Regulations/Orders, etc. laid on th e Table 
of the House should be invariably uploaded on the 
websites of respective Ministries immediately on th e same 
day when they have been laid on the Table of the Ho use, 

for information of Members of Parliament and people  at 
large for their easy access.”

enacting laws is defeated if rules are not framed a nd laid

improving this position.   The Committee hopes that 
Ministry would strive to keep the delay to the mini mum 
and take care that Notifications are laid on the Ta ble of 
the House at the first available opportunity after

2.  While scrutinizing these Orders, the Committee note d 
that there was a considerable time lag between issu e  of 
Notifications and their laying in some cases. The a nnexed 
statement also indicates the period of delay in cas es where 
Notifications have not been laid as per the time sc hedule 
prescribed by the Committee. The Committee observed  that 
out of the total 105 delayed Notifications, there w ere 95 
Notifications where no delay statement was appended  to. 
However, the bulk of delayed Notifications were fro m the 
Ministry of  Road Transport and Highways which come s to 
around 23.8% of the total delayed Notifications. 
 

The observations/recommendations of the Committee 
in respect of the specific Ministries/Departments w here delay 
in laying of Notifications has been noticed, are as follows: -  
 
(i) Ministry of  Civil Aviation  
  
 Ministry of Civil Aviation   have laid 3 Notificat ions 
(Sl. Nos. 23 to 26). Only 1 Notification (Sl. No. 2 3) has been 
delayed by 5 Months and there is no delay statement  
appended to it.  
  
   The Committee notes that although there has been 
delay in laying of only one Notification yet no del ay 
statement has been attached to it. The Committee 
reiterates its recommendation contained in its 135 
th  
Report that in case of delay in laying of Notificat ions etc., 
invariably a delay statement should be attached. Th e 
Ministry of Civil Aviation should ensure such compl iance 
in future.  
 
(ii)  Ministry of Commerce and Industry 
 (Department of Industrial Policy and Promotion)  
 
 The Ministry of  Commerce and Industry(Department 
of Industrial Policy and Promotion) have laid 4 Not ifications 
(Sl. Nos. 31 – 34). Out of these, one Notification (Sl. No. 31) 
has been delayed by 11 months, which is  accompanied with a 
delay statement. The reasons of delay given by the Ministry is 
as under:- 
 
 “The reason for delay in laying the Notification S .O. 
178 (E) [Enerty Efficient Induction Motors-Three Ph ase 
Squirrel Cage (Quality Control) Order, 2017] dated 18 
th  
January, 2017 on the Table of Lok Sabh/Rajya Sabha is due 

to unavoidable delay occurred in the process of ame ndment 
initiated, after receiving various representation f or 
amendment in the order, under frequent consultation  of 
various stakeholders which was to be done before th e 
effective date of the order i.e. 01.10.2017.” 
 
The Committee hopes that the Ministry of 
Commerce and Industry (Department of Industrial Pol icy 
and Promotion) would avoid such instances of delay in 
laying of subordinate legislation in future and wou ld 
remove lacuna, if any, unavoidable, administrative or 
otherwise, causing delay. The Committee also impres ses 
upon the Ministry to take note of the fact that in case 
there is a delay in the laying of any Statutory Not ification, 
the same should be accompanied by a delay statement  
while it is being laid . The Committee also advises the 
Ministry to avoid recurrence of delays due to unavo idable 
reasons. 
 
(iii) Ministry of Communications 
 (Department of Telecommunications) 
 
 Ministry of Communications (Department of 
Telecommunications)  have laid 9 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 36 to 
44) out of which only 1 Notification (Sl. No. 36) h as been 
delayed by 9 months and appended delay statement th ereto. 
The reasons for delay given by the Ministry is that  due to 
oversight Notifications could not be laid on the Ta ble of the 
House. 
 
 The Committee cannot appreciate the reasons 
given by the Ministry of Communications (Department  of 
Telecommunications) that Notifications could not be  laid 
on the Table of the House due to oversight. This is  sheer 

lackadaisical approach on the part of the Ministry to have 
neglected its constitutional responsibility. This a pproach 
calls for relook/introspection so as to bring impro vement 
in the current situation. 
 
 
 
(iv) Ministry of Corporate Affairs 
 
 The Ministry of Corporate Affairs have laid 31 
Notifications (Sl. Nos. 52 to 82). Out of these, on e 
Notification (Sl. No. 69) has been delayed by 5 mon ths with 
delay statement appended thereto. The reason for de lay given 
by the Ministry is as under:- 
 
 “The Notification relating to the G.S.R. No. 955 ( E) 
dated 27.07.2017 on Companies (Incorporation) Secon d 
Amendment Rules, 2017 was required to be laid befor e both 
the Houses of Parliament during the Monsoon Session, 2017. 
 The above Notification G.S.R. No. 955 (E) dated 
27.07.2017 on Companies (Incorporation) Second 
Amendment Rules, 2017 was sent to Government Press for 
printing. The said notification could not be laid b efore both 
the Houses of Parliament during the Monsoon Session  of the 
Parliament, 2017 as e-Gazette copy of the said noti fication 
was not uploaded by the Department of Printing, D/o  
Publication and when it was uploaded both Sessions of Rajya 
Sabha and Lok Sabha were over on 11.08.2017. The sa id 
notification got delayed and hence it may be kindly  be 
condoned.” 
 
The Committee does not accept that the e-Gazette 
copy of the said notification was not uploaded by t he 
Department of Printing, D/o Publication as a valid reason 

for  delayed laying of Notifications etc. The Commi ttee 
does not accept this as a convincing reason in resp ect of 
laying of statutory papers before the Parliament. T he 
Ministry of Corporate Affairs  should, therefore,  in 
future ensure that all its papers are laid before t he House 
within the time frame as prescribed in the Committe e’s 
131 st  Report. 
 
The Committee, therefore,  otherwise also, 
reiterates its earlier direction to all the Ministr ies that in 
case there is delay in procuring printed copies in time, 
they may obtain G.S.R. and S.O. numbers from the 
Government of India Press and prepare requisite num ber 
of copies in cyclostyled form for laying in the Par liament 
as suggested by Secretary, Ministry of  Urban 
Development, the controlling Ministry of Government  of 
India Press, in its meeting held on 30  July, 2013.  The 
Committee also once again recommends that this proc ess 
may be adopted by Ministries suo moto  on immediate 
basis so as to avoid such delays henceforth. 
 
(v) Ministry of Defence 
 
 The Ministry of Defence have laid 17 Notifications  
(Sl. Nos. 83 to 99) on the Table of the House durin g the 
Session. Out of these, 16 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 8 3 to 98) 
have been delayed. None of these have delay stateme nts 
appended thereto and  the delay period ranges from 6 months 
to 8 months.  
   
 The Committee takes a serious note of the fact tha t 
the percentage of delayed Notifications, out of tot al 
Notifications laid, is quite high i.e. as high as o ver 94.1%. 
This is simply unacceptable. Further, the Ministry have 

not appended any delay statement with any of the  
delayed Notifications/Rules. Ministry of Defence sh ould 
look into the matter seriously to eliminate recurre nce of 
such delays in completing the procedural formalitie s. The 
Committee expects that the Ministry of  Defence sho uld 
adhere to the time schedule in laying of Notificati ons as 
prescribed in the Committee’s 131 
st  Report and append a 
delay statement without fail in case there is  dela y in 
laying. This has, sort of, become a matter of routi ne with 
Ministries, its seems. The Ministry may clarify the reasons 
for delay in laying and also why the delay statemen t has 
not been appended to the Notifications. 
 
(iv) Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate 
Change 
 
 Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change  
have laid 5 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 100 to 104) dur ing the 
Session. Out of these two Notifications (Sl. Nos. 1 00 & 102) 
have been delayed. One of them  (Sl. No. 100) has b een 
delayed by 21 months and another has been delayed b y 5 
months and no delay statement is appended to both o f these 
delayed Notifications. 
 
The Committee is constrained to note  that 2 out of   
5 Notifications laid by the Ministry of Environment , 
Forest and Climate Change, on the Table of the Hous e, 
were not only delayed by 7 months to 21 months, 
respectively,  but also did not have any delay stat ement 
attached to them.  
As a result, Committee is not aware of the reason f or this 
delay. The Committee views this very seriously and feels 
that not appending the delay statements is akin to 
infringement of Parliament’s right to know the fact s of 

the case. Hence, the Committee reiterates  its 
recommendations, as contained in its 131 
st  and 135 th  
Reports, emphasizing timely laying of  Notification s  on 
the Table of the House and appending a delay statem ent 
wherever there has been a delay.  
 
(vii) Ministry of External Affairs 
 
The Ministry of External Affairs have laid 6 
Notifications (Sl. No. 105 to  110) and all of thes e have been 
delayed. The delay ranges from 6 months to 8 months . 
Moreover, no delay statement have been appended to any of

 The Committee take serious note for delay of

House and advise the Ministry of External Affairs t o take 
necessary steps to obviate such delays and remove l acuna,

delay in the laying of any Statutory Notifications,  the 
same should be accompanied by a delay statement whi le it

Committee hopes that Ministry of Finance (Departmen t 
of Economic Affairs) would take adequate precaution s to 
avoid such instances of delay in future and would 
invariable append a delay statement in case of dela y in 
laying on the Table of the House.

th

The Committee expresses its anguish on the fact 
that the only Notification that Ministry of Rural 
Development (Department of Rural Development) have 
laid, has been delayed by nine months. Further, the re is 
no reason given for this delay.  This is in contrav ention of 
Committee’s recommendation given in its 135 Report that 
Notification which are delayed should invariably be  
accompanied by a delay statement. The Committee wou ld 
like the Ministry of Rural Development (Department of 
Rural Development) to take necessary steps to obvia te 
such delays and, in case of delay in laying of Noti fications, 

a delay statement should invariably be accompanied with 
them. 
 
(xviii) Ministry of Textiles 
  
Ministry of Textiles have laid 8 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 
667 to 674) on the Table of the House during the Se ssion. 
Two of them  (Sl. Nos. 667 & 670) have been delayed  by 6 to 
9 months and no delay statement is appended to both  of these 
delayed Notifications. 
 
 The Committee takes a strong view of the delay 
occurred in tabling the Notifications in time and 
emphasise that the Ministry should avoid such insta nces 
of delay in laying of Subordinate Legislation in fu ture. 
The Committee also impresses upon the Ministry to t ake 
note of the fact that in case, there is a delay in the laying 
of any Statutory Notifications, the same should be 
accompanied by a delay statement while it is being laid. 
The Ministry may clarify the reasons for delay in l aying 
and also why the delay statement has not been appen ded 
to the Notifications. 
 
3.   The Committee impresses upon all the 
Ministries/Departments to take immediate and concre te steps 
to ensure timely and proper laying of subordinate l egislation. 
The Committee, accordingly, wishes to bring to the notice of 
all Ministries/Departments of the Government of Ind ia, 
particularly, the defaulting ones, the following 
recommendations, as contained in its 7 
th , 10 th , 131 
st 
, 135 
th 
, 
152 
nd ,  192 nd  , 201 st , 212 th  and 213 th  Reports: 
 

 “The Committee desires that for the convenience 
of the public and Members, Ministries should hencef orth 
send copies of 'order' duly authenticated by the Mi nisters 
concerned, incorporating therein all the correction s and 
amendments issued till date of laying such 'orders' instead 
of laying the uncorrected copy along with corrigend a. The 
Committee feels that to obviate any legal or techni cal 
difficulty, Ministries should examine whether there  is any 
necessity of assigning a separate G.S.R. No. to a 
corrigendum at the time of its publication in the G azette 
and whether such a corrigendum should not be publis hed 
without assigning any G.S.R. No. The Committee woul d, 
therefore, like to impress upon all Ministries of t he 
Government of India that the present practice of la ying 
the rules without incorporating corrigenda in the b ody of 
the rules is not a healthy one. The Committee hopes  that 
the Ministries will ensure supply of only corrected  copies 
of the rules for laying on the Table so that they d epict a 
true and correct picture and serve the desired purp ose." 
  
(7 
th   Report) 
(Presented on 12 th   May, 1969) 
 
 The Committee approve the following draft revised 
formula for laying of Statutory Rules before both H ouses 
of Parliament which the Ministry of Law and Justice  
propose to incorporate in all future legislation wh ich 
provide for making of rules by the CentralGovernment:— 
 
 "Every rule made by the Central Government under 
this Act shall be laid, as soon as may be after it is 
made, before each House of Parliament, while it is in 
session, for a total period of thirty days which ma y be 
comprised in one session or in two or more successi ve 

sessions, and if, before the expiry of the session 
immediately following the session or the successive  
sessions aforesaid, both Houses agree in making any  
modification in the rule or both Houses agree that the 
rule should not be made, the rule shall thereafter 
have effect only in such modified form or be of no 
effect, as the case may be; so, however that any su ch 
modification or annulment shall be without prejudic e 
to the validity of anything previously done under t hat 
rule." 
  
 The Committee recommend that the revised 
formula should be incorporated not only in new 
legislation but also in the existing Acts as and wh en Bills 
to amend them are brought before Parliament. The 
Ministry should also incorporate the new formula in  the 
Bills pending before Parliament. This will, in the opinion 
of the Committee, bring about uniformity in the mat ter 
expeditiously. 
(10 
th   Report) 
(presented on 24 th  May, 1971) 
 
 
 “Orders required to be laid before the House shoul d 
be laid (i) if the House is not in Session, during the Session 
immediately following the date of publication of the Order 
in the Official Gazette and (ii) if the House is in  Session, 
on the date of the publication of the Order, during  its 
continuance and in case the time lag between the da te of 
publication and the date of the closing of the Sess ion is 
less than 15 clear days, before the expiry of the S ession 
immediately following the said Session. All the 
Ministries/Departments of Government of India shoul d 
henceforth comply with this schedule in the matter of 

laying of the Orders issued under various Acts of 
Parliament on the Table of the Rajya Sabha. 
 
(131 st  Report) 
(Presented on 15 
th   December 2000) 
 
 “The Committee has, time and again, emphasized 
that it is essential that in case there is a delay in the laying 
of Statutory Orders, the concerned Ministry/Departm ent 
should invariably append a delay statement along with the 
Notifications being laid so as to apprise Parliamen t of the 
causes of delay. The Committee desires all 
Ministries/Departments to take a note of this, sinc e the 
intention is that through the process of formulatio n of a 
delay statement, the Ministry is able to introspect, identify 
bottlenecks and devise remedial measures”. 
(135 th  Report) 
(Presented on 27 
th   July 2001) 
 
 “In the opinion of the Committee, every notificati on 
should be assigned a distinctive number in order to  give it 
a separate identity and similarly, no notification should be 
published/laid which does not carry a notification 
number. The Committee expects all 
Ministries/Departments of Government of India to 
exercise caution in this regard. In case where ther e are 
more than one Notifications under a single file, th e 
Ministries/Departments should ensure that the file 
number on each notification should be suitably 
distinguished from one another.” 
(152 
nd 
 Report) 
(Presented on 26 th   August 2004)  
 

 “In addition to the concern expressed by the 
Committee over delay in laying of Notifications on the 
Table of the House, the Committee also express thei r deep 
concern over delay in framing of rules/regulations under 
different Acts. The Committee in its 47 
th  report presented 
to the House on 14.9.1981 has recommended that the rule-
making process should be completed within a period of six 
months of the coming into force of an Act. The Committee 
has further recommended that in case a Ministry is not 
able to adhere to this time limit, it should seek e xtension 
of time for completing the rule-making process. The  
recommendation of the committee reads as follows:- 
 
  “The Committee feels that the rule-
making process could well have been completed 
within the time limit of six months which the 
Committee has laid down for making of rules 
under an Act after coming into force of that Act. 
Where however, a Ministry does not find it possible 
to adhere to the time limit, they should inform the  
Committee of the reasons why they cannot make 
rules within the time limit and seek extension of 
time for completing the rule-making process.” 
  
 The Committee is constrained to take note of the 
fact that the Ministries/Departments of Government of 
India are not complying with the Committee’s 
recommendation to complete the process of framing o f 
subordinate legislation contemplated under various Acts 
of Parliament within a period of six months. At the  same 
time, the Committee also does not receive requests for 
extension of time for completing the rule-making pr ocess 
in terms of its recommendations as above from most of 

the Ministries/Departments. The Committee takes a 
serious note of the prevailing situation in which t he 
Ministries/Departments are neither able to complete  the 
task of framing rules/regulations under different A cts 
within the given six months’ period nor do they suo-motu  
approach the Committee for seeking extension of tim e. 
The Committee further notes that in order to ensure  
timely framing of rules/regulations it has taken an  
initiative to monitor the progress of framing of 
subordinate legislation in respect of all legislati ons 
brought about by different Ministries/Departments o f 
Government of India from the year 2003 onwards with  a 
view to ensure that the framing of subordinate legi slation 
is not delayed. The Committee, however, finds that the 
responses from the Ministries/Departments have not been 
prompt in this monitoring exercise undertaken on be half 
of the Committee. 
  
 In view of the above position, the Committee once 
again reiterates its recommendation that the 
Ministries/Departments should ensure putting in pla ce 
subordinate legislation positively within a period of six 
months of coming into force of the Act. The Committ ee 
further recommends that in case the Ministry fails to meet 
with this deadline, they should invariably approach  the 
Committee for seeking extension of time. The Commit tee 
further recommends that in cases where the time lim it of 
six months is not adhered to, they should, while la ying 
rules/regulations before the Parliament invariably lay a 
statement explaining the reasons why the framing of  
rules/regulations was delayed beyond six months so as to 
keep the Parliament apprised of the compliance of t he 
Parliament’s mandate  conferred upon the Executive.” 

(192 
nd 
 Report) 
(Presented on 26 th   August 2011)  
 
  Rules/Regulations/Orders/bye-laws are laid by 
different Ministries on the Table of the House unde r 
various provisions of parent Acts passed by Parliam ent. 
These Rules/ Regulations/Orders/bye-laws are publis hed 
in the official Gazette before being laid on the Table of the 
House. Even after they are laid, it is very difficu lt to get 
access to these Notifications. The Committee recomm ends 
that such Rules/Regulations/Orders, etc. laid on th e Table 
of the House should be invariably uploaded on the 
websites of respective Ministries immediately on th e same 
day when they have been laid on the Table of the Ho use, 
for information of Members of Parliament and people  at 
large for their easy access. 
201 
st  Report 
(Presented on 14 th  December, 2012)  
 
The Committee observes that the whole process of 
enacting laws is defeated if rules are not framed a nd laid 
on the Table of the House in time.  A reasonable de lay 
could be understood but unjustifiably long delays s hould 
be avoided and the Ministries should work towards 
improving this position.   The Committee hopes that 
Ministry would strive to keep the delay to the mini mum 
and take care that Notifications are laid on the Ta ble of 
the House at the first available opportunity after 
publication of Notifications. 
 
The Committee would like to impress upon the 
Ministry that it is their responsibility to ensure that copies 
of the Notifications are printed timely and for thi s 

purpose, they need to evolve a suitable mechanism t o 
ensure that notifications are laid in time.   The C ommittee 
is happy that the Ministry has evolved an internal 
mechanism/ procedure for this purpose.  The Committ ee 
hopes that it would take action accordingly in orde r to 
comply with the prescribed schedule in the matter o f 
laying of statutory Notifications. 
 
The Ministry must take appropriate step to 
remove lacuna, if any, administrative or otherwise,  
causing such long delay by being little proactive a nd 
prompt.  Further, the Ministries should take it up with the 
Ministry of Urban Development for late receiving of  
printed copies of the Notification. 
212 
th   Report 
(Presented on  3 rd  September, 2013) 
 
 “The Committee is not inclined to accept the late 
availability of printed copies of Notifications fro m the 
Government of India Press as the reason for delay i n 
laying of the Notifications. The Committee directs all the 
Ministries that in case there is a delay in procuri ng 
printed copies in time, they may obtain G.S.R. and S.O. 
numbers from the Government of India Press and 
prepare requisite number of copies in cyclostyled form for 
laying in the Parliament. The Committee also 
recommends that this process may be adopted by 
Ministries suo moto  on immediate basis so as to avoid such 
delays henceforth”. 
213 
th   Report 
(Presented on  19 th  February, 2014)

 The Committee approve the following draft revised 
formula for laying of Statutory Rules before both H ouses 
of Parliament which the Ministry of Law and Justice  
propose to incorporate in all future legislation wh ich 
provide for making of rules by the CentralGovernment:— 
 
 "Every rule made by the Central Government under 
this Act shall be laid, as soon as may be after it is 
made, before each House of Parliament, while it is in 
session, for a total period of thirty days which ma y be 
comprised in one session or in two or more successi ve 
sessions, and if, before the expiry of the session 
immediately following the session or the successive  
sessions aforesaid, both Houses agree in making any  
modification in the rule or both Houses agree that the 
rule should not be made, the rule shall thereafter 
have effect only in such modified form or be of no 

effect, as the case may be; so, however that any su ch 
modification or annulment shall be without prejudic e 
to the validity of anything previously done under t hat 
rule." 
  
The Committee recommend that the revised formula 
should be incorporated not only in new legislation but also 
in the existing Acts as and when Bills to amend the m are 
brought before Parliament. The Ministry should also  
incorporate the new formula in the Bills pending be fore 
Parliament. This will, in the opinion of the Commit tee, 
bring about uniformity in the matter expeditiously.
