2.  While scrutinizing these Orders, the Committee note d 
that there was a considerable time lag between issu e  of 
Notifications and their laying in some cases. The a nnexed 
statement also indicates the period of delay in cas es where 
Notifications have not been laid as per the time sc hedule 
prescribed by the Committee. The Committee observed  that 
out of the total 67 delayed Notifications, there we re 52 
Notifications where no delay statement was appended  to. The 
bulk of delayed Notifications were from the Ministr y of  
Road Transport and Highways which comes to around 4 6.2% 
of the total delayed Notifications. 
 

The observations/recommendations of the Committee 
in respect of the specific Ministries/Departments w here delay 
in laying of Notifications has been noticed, are as follows: -  
 
(i) Ministry of Health & Family Welfare 
 (Department of Health & Family Welfare) 
 
 The Ministry of Health & Family Welfare 
(Department of Health & Family Welfare)   have laid 17 
Notifications (Sl. Nos. 316 to 332) on the Table of  the 
Council during the Session, and  11 Notification ha ve been 
delayed.  7 Notification (Sl. Nos. 324 – 330) have been laid 
with huge delay period ranging from 5 years 8 month s to 36 
years and 8 months though all of them have been 
accompanied with delay statements. Whereas 4 other  
Notifications have been delayed by 4 months to 10 m onths 
and there is no delay statement attached thereto. T he reasons 
cited by the Ministry for delay are  as under:- 
 
 “As per the provision 29(3) of the All India Insti tute 
of Medical Sciences, Act, 1956 every regulation mad e under 
this section shall be laid, as soon as may be after  it is made, 
before each House of Parliament, while it is in ses sion, for a 
total period of thirty days, which may be comprised  in one 
session or in two or more successive sessions, and if, before 
the expiry of the sessions immediately following th e sessions 
or the successive sessions aforesaid, both Houses a gree in 
making any modifications in the regulation or both Houses 
agree that the regulation should not be made, the r egulation 
shall thereafter have effect only in such modified form or be 
of no effect, as the case may be, so however that a ny such 
modification or annulment shall be without prejudic e to the 
validity of anything previously done under that regulation. 

 Delay in laying the Regulation in both the Houses of 
Parliament has occurred due to oversight in the Ins titute. The 
said delay is sincerely regretted.”  
 
 This Committee regrets to say that there is delay in 
laying of almost 64.7% of Notifications that the Mi nistry 
of Health & Family Welfare (Department of Health & 
Family Welfare) have laid. Further 4 Notifications have a 
long and undue delay ranging from fifteen years two  
months to thirty-six years and ten months,  3 Notif ications 
have a delay period ranging from five years and eig hth 
months to eight years and eighth months and 4 
Notifications have a delay period of five months to  ten 
months! The Committee cannot simply accept the reas on 
given by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare  
(Department of Health)  that the Notifications could not be 
laid on time due to oversight. This is not comprehe nsible 
as how this inordinate delay can happen due to over sight. 
The delay period is very high. Furthermore, there i s no 
delay statement appended to any of these delayed 
Notifications which is again unacceptable. No delay  
statement coupled with inordinate delay is quite enigmatic 
to the Committee. The Committee always makes a poin t 
that Ministry should have appended a delay statemen t so 
as to apprise the Parliament of the reasons of dela y in 
laying of Notifications on the Table of the Houses.  The  
Ministry of Health & Family Welfare (Department of 
Health & Family Welfare) should inquire the excessi ve 
delay period in laying of the Notifications and tak e 
corrective steps. The Committee reiterates its 
recommendations as contained in its 131 
st  and 135 th  
Reports emphasizing timely laying of  Notifications   on 
the Table of the Council and appending a delay stat ement 
wherever there has been a delay. Not appending a de lay 

statement is akin to infringement of Parliament’s r ight to 
know the facts of the case. The Committee takes a s erious 
note of the matter and urges the Ministry to be car eful in 
future.   
 
(ii)  Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate 
Change 
  
 Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change  
have laid 12 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 85 to 96) duri ng the 
Session. Out of these 5 Notifications, (Sl. Nos. 86  - 90) have 
been delayed by 6 months to 1 year and 5 months and  no 
delay statement is attached to any of the delayed 
Notifications.  
   
 The Committee are pained to notice that out of 12 
Notifications which Ministry of Environment, Forest  and 
Climate Change have laid, five Notifications have b een 
delayed from 6 months to 17 months. Further, there is no 
reason given for this inordinate delay.  This is in  
contravention to Committee’s recommendation given i n 
its 135 
th  Report that Notifications which are delayed 
should invariably be accompanied by delay statement s. 
The Committee would like the Ministry of Environmen t, 
Forest and Climate Change to take necessary steps t o 
obviate such delays and in case of delay in laying of 
Notifications, a delay statement should invariably be 
appended with them.  
 
(iii) Ministry of  Home Affairs 
 
Ministry of Home Affairs  have laid 15 Notification s 
(Sl. No. 333 to 347). Two of them (Sl. No. 333 and 334) have 
been delayed by 11 months and 9 months respectively and are 

accompanied with delay statement. The reason given by the 
Ministry for delay is as under:-. 
 
 “The Notification No. 266/2017/F.No. 27-4/2014-
Rev. dated 06.11.2017 (English version) in respect of 
‘the Andaman and Nicobar Islands Anand Marriage 
Registration Rule, 2017’ and Notification No. 
ADM/LAW/29/2017/1747 DATED 04.09.2017 
(English version) in respect of  ‘the Dadra and Nag ar 
Haveli Anand Marriages Registration Rules, 2017’ 
were published by UT Administrations of Andaman & 
Nicobar Islands and Dadra and Nagar Haveli 
respectively under section 6 of the Anand Marriage 
Act, 1909 (7 of 1909) as amended by the Anand 
Marriage (Amendment) Act, 2012 (29 of 2012). The 
notification could not be laid on the table of the 
Houses due to the delay in the publication of the Hindi 
version of the Notification by the UT Administration. 
 
 The Hindi version of Notification No. 266/2017/F.N o. 
27-4/2014-Rev. dated 06.11.2017 & 
ADM/LAW/29/2017/1747 DATED 04.09.2017 have 
now been published in the Gazette of Andaman & 
Nicobar Islands and Dadra & Nagar Haveli and 
received in  this Ministry only on 14.05.2016 and 
22.05.2018 in respect of A&NI and DNH 
respectively. Hence Notification (both in Hindi & 
English version) are being laid on the Table of Lok  
Sabha/Rajya Sabha under Section 6(4) of the Anand 
Marriage Act, 1909 (7 of 1909) as amended by the 
Anand Marriage (Amendment) Act, 2012 (29 of 
2012). The aforesaid Hindi version of notifications got 
delayed and which caused further delay in laying th e 
copies (Hindi and English version) to both the Hous es 

of Parliament and it is requested that the same may  
kindly be condoned.” 
 
 The Committee notes with deep concern the delay 
of eleven  months and nine months in laying of the 
Notifications.  The Committee finds that laying of the 
notifications was delayed due to late receipt of th e Hindi 
version of Notification No. 266/2017/F.No. 27-4/201 4-Rev. 
dated 06.11.2017 & ADM/LAW/29/2017/1747 DATED 
04.09.2017 and have now been published in the Gazet te of 
Andaman & Nicobar Islands and Dadra & Nagar Haveli 
and excessive time has been taken in completing the  
procedural formalities in the Ministry of Home Affairs. In 
this context the Committee observes that it is the 
Ministry’s responsibility to ensure that the Subord inate 
Legislation is laid before the Parliament within th e 
prescribed time schedule and accordingly, it is for  the 
Ministry only to ensure that they receive the same timely 
from the statutory bodies under them and complete a ll 
formalities of laying them before the Council is 
adjourned. The Committee recommends that the Ministry 
of Home Affairs may take necessary remedial measures to 
ensure that papers are laid well in time  on the Ta ble of 
the Council. 
 
(iv) Ministry of Road Transport and Highways 
 
The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways have 
laid 84 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 380 to 463). There has been 
significant number of Notifications which have been  delayed. 
Out of 27 delayed Notifications only 4 Notification s (Sl. Nos. 
380 -383) have been attached with delay statement a nd 23 
Notifications have no delay statement appended ther eto. The 
delay period ranges from 5 to 9 months. The reasons given by 

the Ministry is that it took some time to collect the papers and 
complete the procedural formalities. Therefore, Not ifications 
could not be laid in time on the Table of both the Houses of 
Parliament. 
 
The Committee is constrained to observe that 
delay in laying Notifications in such large number is just 
not acceptable to the Committee. Moreover, 23 out o f 27 
Notifications delayed did not have the delay statem ents 
appended thereto. While there may be a reason for t he 
delay, but there cannot be any reason for not furni shing 
reason for that. The Ministry must understand the 
implications for not doing so regularly more so in such a 
large number of cases. 
 
 The Committee does not accept the reasons of the 
delay given by the  Ministry of Road Transport and 
Highways that it took some time to collect the pape rs and 
complete the procedural formalities. The Committee 
wonders how can it take such a long time to receive  
Notifications and to complete procedural formalitie s. The 
Committee feels that the Ministry did not take adeq uate 
precaution to avoid the delay. The Committee furthe r 
makes a point that Ministry should append a delay 
statement in each such cases so as to apprise the 
Parliament of the reasons of delay in laying of 
Notifications on the Table of the Houses. 
 
 
(v) Ministry of  Electronics and Information 
Technology  
  
Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology 
have laid 8 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 77 to 84) . Out  of  these  

one  Notification ( Sl. No. 83) have been delayed b y 7 
months. There is no delay statement appended thereto. 
 
The Committee takes a serious view of not only the 
delay in laying of one of its Notifications on the Table of 
the Council but also failure to append a delay stat ement 
with it. The Ministry of Electronics and Informatio n 
Technology must know about the possible implication s of 
failing to meet this requirement. The Committee 
recommends that the  Ministry of  Electronics and 
Information Technology ensure to append a delay 
statement in all such cases in future . 
 
(vi) Ministry of Finance

Services) have laid 11 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 134 to 144), out 
of which 4 Notifications have been delayed.  Out of 4 delayed 
Notifications,  2  Notifications (Sl. Nos. 141 & 14 2) have  
been delayed each by 5 months and have no delay sta tements 
attached to either of them. 2 Notifications (Sl. No s. 137 & 
138) have been delayed  by 6 months with delay stat ement 
appended to both of them. The reasons forwarded by the 
Ministry for delay is as under:- 
 
 “The Notifications dated 29.6.2017 regarding 
amendment in Canara Bank Employees’ Pension 
Regulations, 1995 and Canara Bank Officers’ Service  
Regulations, 1979 were published in the Gazette of 
India, vide No. 2 & 4 dated January 13 – January, 1 9,

However, as the Notification  numbers and name of 
the Bank was not appearing on the first page of the  
publication, revised copies could be sent vide thei r 
letter dated 12.4.2018 and 3.5.2018. The Bank has 
submitted that the delay is not intentional and 
requested that the same may kindly be condoned. 
 
In view of above, the said Notifications could not be 
laid on the Table  of the both the Houses on earlie r 
occasions. Delay in this regard is  deeply regrette d and 
may please be condoned.” 
 
The Committee takes a serious view not only about 
the delay in laying of ten Notifications  by the Mi nistry of 
Finance (Department of Financial Services) on the T able 
of the Council but also of  its failure to append t he 
required delay statement. The Committee observes th at 
Parliamentary sessions are declared much in advance  and 
had the Ministry of Finance (Department of Financia l 
Services) taken prompt steps for laying of the 
notifications, in coordination with Banks for suppl y of 
Gazette Notifications in right form,  the delay cou ld have 
been well avoided. It reflects management/planning on the 
part of the Ministry. The Committee, therefore, 
recommends that the Ministry should complete the 
procedural formalities at the earliest to avoid suc h kind of 
delays in future and invariably attach the delay st atement 
when there is delay in laying the Notification.

 Ministry of Finance (Department of revenue) have

th   

Session. Out of these 7 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 167   & 214 –

 The Committee appreciates that the Ministry of

in its 131 
st  and 135 th  Reports emphasizing timely laying of

appending delay statement is akin to infringement o f

Ministry of Power  have laid 4 Notifications (Sl. N os.

appended to all of  these delayed Notifications. 
 
 The Committee takes a strong view of the delay

The Committee also impresses upon the Ministry to t ake 
note of the fact that in case there is a delay in t he laying of

The Ministry may take steps to avoid delay in layin g and

 (viii) Ministry of Science and Technology 
 (Department of Science and Technology) 
 
 Only one Notification that the Ministry of Science  and 
Technology (Department of Science and Technology) ( Sl. 
No. 464) have laid was delayed by 5 months and no d elay

 The Committee is unhappy over the delay in laying

Technology (Department of Science and Technology)   by  
5 months. Further, there is no delay statement appe nded 
thereto giving reasons as to what caused such undue

 Ministry of Textiles have laid 7 Notifications (Sl . Nos.

– 476) have been

 The Committee is concerned over the delay in

particularly Notifications at Sl. Nos. 475 and 476 where

3.   The Committee impresses upon all the 
Ministries/Departments to take immediate and concre te steps 
to ensure timely and proper laying of subordinate l egislation. 
The Committee, accordingly, wishes to bring to the notice of 
all Ministries/Departments of the Government of Ind ia, 
particularly, the defaulting ones, the following 
recommendations, as contained in its 7 
th , 10 th , 131 
st 
, 135 
th 
, 
152 
nd ,  192 nd  , 201 st , 212 th  and 213 th  Reports: 
 
 “The Committee desires that for the convenience 
of the public and Members, Ministries should hencef orth 
send copies of 'order' duly authenticated by the Mi nisters 
concerned, incorporating therein all the correction s and 
amendments issued till date of laying such 'orders' instead 
of laying the uncorrected copy along with corrigend a. The 
Committee feels that to obviate any legal or techni cal 
difficulty, Ministries should examine whether there  is any 
necessity of assigning a separate G.S.R. No. to a 
corrigendum at the time of its publication in the G azette 
and whether such a corrigendum should not be publis hed 
without assigning any G.S.R. No. The Committee woul d, 
therefore, like to impress upon all Ministries of t he 
Government of India that the present practice of la ying 

the rules without incorporating corrigenda in the b ody of 
the rules is not a healthy one. The Committee hopes  that 
the Ministries will ensure supply of only corrected  copies 
of the rules for laying on the Table so that they d epict a 
true and correct picture and serve the desired purp ose." 
  
(7 th   Report) 
(Presented on 12 th   May, 1969) 
 
 The Committee approve the following draft revised 
formula for laying of Statutory Rules before both H ouses 
of Parliament which the Ministry of Law and Justice  
propose to incorporate in all future legislation wh ich 
provide for making of rules by the Central 
Government:— 
 
 "Every rule made by the Central Government under 
this Act shall be laid, as soon as may be after it is 
made, before each House of Parliament, while it is in 
session, for a total period of thirty days which ma y be 
comprised in one session or in two or more successi ve 
sessions, and if, before the expiry of the session 
immediately following the session or the successive  
sessions aforesaid, both Houses agree in making any  
modification in the rule or both Houses agree that the 
rule should not be made, the rule shall thereafter 
have effect only in such modified form or be of no 
effect, as the case may be; so, however that any su ch 
modification or annulment shall be without prejudic e 
to the validity of anything previously done under t hat 
rule." 
  
The Committee recommend that the revised formula 
should be incorporated not only in new legislation but also 

in the existing Acts as and when Bills to amend the m are 
brought before Parliament. The Ministry should also  
incorporate the new formula in the Bills pending be fore 
Parliament. This will, in the opinion of the Commit tee, 
bring about uniformity in the matter expeditiously. 
 
(10 th   Report) 
(presented on 24 th  May, 1971) 
 
 
 “Orders required to be laid before the House shoul d 
be laid (i) if the House is not in Session, during the Session 
immediately following the date of publication of the Order 
in the Official Gazette and (ii) if the House is in  Session, 
on the date of the publication of the Order, during  its 
continuance and in case the time lag between the da te of 
publication and the date of the closing of the Sess ion is 
less than 15 clear days, before the expiry of the S ession 
immediately following the said Session. All the 
Ministries/Departments of Government of India shoul d 
henceforth comply with this schedule in the matter of 
laying of the Orders issued under various Acts of 
Parliament on the Table of the Rajya Sabha. 
 
(131 st  Report) 
(Presented on 15 
th   December 2000) 
 
 
 
 “The Committee has, time and again, emphasized 
that it is essential that in case there is a delay in the laying 
of Statutory Orders, the concerned Ministry/Departm ent 
should invariably append a delay statement along with the 

Notifications being laid so as to apprise Parliamen t of the 
causes of delay. The Committee desires all 
Ministries/Departments to take a note of this, sinc e the 
intention is that through the process of formulatio n of a 
delay statement, the Ministry is able to introspect, identify 
bottlenecks and devise remedial measures”. 
(135 th  Report) 
(Presented on 27 
th   July 2001) 
 
 “In the opinion of the Committee, every notificati on 
should be assigned a distinctive number in order to  give it 
a separate identity and similarly, no notification should be 
published/laid which does not carry a notification 
number. The Committee expects all 
Ministries/Departments of Government of India to 
exercise caution in this regard. In case where ther e are 
more than one Notifications under a single file, th e 
Ministries/Departments should ensure that the file 
number on each notification should be suitably 
distinguished from one another.” 
(152 
nd 
 Report) 
(Presented on 26 th   August 2004)  
 
 “In addition to the concern expressed by the 
Committee over delay in laying of Notifications on the 
Table of the House, the Committee also express thei r deep 
concern over delay in framing of rules/regulations under 
different Acts. The Committee in its 47 
th  report presented 
to the House on 14.9.1981 has recommended that the rule-
making process should be completed within a period of six 
months of the coming into force of an Act. The Committee 
has further recommended that in case a Ministry is not 

able to adhere to this time limit, it should seek e xtension 
of time for completing the rule-making process. The  
recommendation of the committee reads as follows:- 
 
  “The Committee feels that the rule-
making process could well have been completed 
within the time limit of six months which the 
Committee has laid down for making of rules 
under an Act after coming into force of that Act. 
Where however, a Ministry does not find it possible 
to adhere to the time limit, they should inform the  
Committee of the reasons why they cannot make 
rules within the time limit and seek extension of 
time for completing the rule-making process.” 
  
 The Committee is constrained to take note of the 
fact that the Ministries/Departments of Government of 
India are not complying with the Committee’s 
recommendation to complete the process of framing o f 
subordinate legislation contemplated under various Acts 
of Parliament within a period of six months. At the  same 
time, the Committee also does not receive requests for 
extension of time for completing the rule-making pr ocess 
in terms of its recommendations as above from most of 
the Ministries/Departments. The Committee takes a 
serious note of the prevailing situation in which t he 
Ministries/Departments are neither able to complete  the 
task of framing rules/regulations under different A cts 
within the given six months’ period nor do they suo-motu  
approach the Committee for seeking extension of tim e. 
The Committee further notes that in order to ensure  
timely framing of rules/regulations it has taken an  
initiative to monitor the progress of framing of 

subordinate legislation in respect of all legislati ons 
brought about by different Ministries/Departments o f 
Government of India from the year 2003 onwards with  a 
view to ensure that the framing of subordinate legi slation 
is not delayed. The Committee, however, finds that the 
responses from the Ministries/Departments have not been 
prompt in this monitoring exercise undertaken on be half 
of the Committee. 
  
 In view of the above position, the Committee once 
again reiterates its recommendation that the 
Ministries/Departments should ensure putting in pla ce 
subordinate legislation positively within a period of six 
months of coming into force of the Act. The Committ ee 
further recommends that in case the Ministry fails to meet 
with this deadline, they should invariably approach  the 
Committee for seeking extension of time. The Commit tee 
further recommends that in cases where the time lim it of 
six months is not adhered to, they should, while la ying 
rules/regulations before the Parliament invariably lay a 
statement explaining the reasons why the framing of  
rules/regulations was delayed beyond six months so as to 
keep the Parliament apprised of the compliance of t he 
Parliament’s mandate  conferred upon the Executive.” 
(192 
nd 
 Report) 
(Presented on 26 th   August 2011)  
 
  Rules/Regulations/Orders/bye-laws are laid by 
different Ministries on the Table of the House unde r 
various provisions of parent Acts passed by Parliam ent. 
These Rules/ Regulations/Orders/bye-laws are publis hed 
in the official Gazette before being laid on the Table of the 
House. Even after they are laid, it is very difficu lt to get 

access to these Notifications. The Committee recomm ends 
that such Rules/Regulations/Orders, etc. laid on th e Table 
of the House should be invariably uploaded on the 
websites of respective Ministries immediately on th e same 
day when they have been laid on the Table of the Ho use, 
for information of Members of Parliament and people  at 
large for their easy access. 
201 
st  Report 
(Presented on 14 th  December, 2012)  
 
 
The Committee observes that the whole process of 
enacting laws is defeated if rules are not framed a nd laid 
on the Table of the House in time.  A reasonable de lay 
could be understood but unjustifiably long delays s hould 
be avoided and the Ministries should work towards 
improving this position.   The Committee hopes that 
Ministry would strive to keep the delay to the mini mum 
and take care that Notifications are laid on the Ta ble of 
the House at the first available opportunity after 
publication of Notifications. 
 
The Committee would like to impress upon the 
Ministry that it is their responsibility to ensure that copies 
of the Notifications are printed timely and for thi s 
purpose, they need to evolve a suitable mechanism t o 
ensure that notifications are laid in time.   The C ommittee 
is happy that the Ministry has evolved an internal 
mechanism/ procedure for this purpose.  The Committ ee 
hopes that it would take action accordingly in orde r to 
comply with the prescribed schedule in the matter o f 
laying of statutory Notifications. 
 

The Ministry must take appropriate step to 
remove lacuna, if any, administrative or otherwise,  
causing such long delay by being little proactive a nd 
prompt.  Further, the Ministries should take it up with the 
Ministry of Urban Development for late receiving of  
printed copies of the Notification.

2. While scrutinizing these Orders, the Committee noted 
that there was a considerable time lag between issue  of 
Notifications and their laying in some cases. The annexed 
statement also indicates the period of delay in cases where 
Notifications have not been laid as per the time schedule 
prescribed by the Committee. The Committee finds that out 
of the 67 delayed Notifications, no delay statement was 
appended to 49 Notifications. The bulk of delayed 
Notifications were from the Ministry of  Home Affairs and 
Ministry of Finance, (both 13 Notifications) which comes to 
around 19.4% of the total delayed Notifications. 
 
The observations/recommendations of the Committee 
in respect of the specific Ministries/Departments where delay 
in laying of Notifications has been noticed, are as follows: -  
 
 
 
 
 
(i) Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare 
 (Department of Agriculture, Cooperation and 
Farmers Welfare) 
 
 The Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare 
(Department of Agriculture, Cooperation and Farmers 
Welfare) laid 9 Notifications (Sl. No. 1 to 9) during the 
Session. Out of these, two Notifications (Sl. Nos. 2 & 9) have 

been delayed by 7 and 6 months respectively and no delay 
statement was attached to any of these Notifications. 
 
 The Committee have clearly mentioned in its 135th 
Report that delay statements should invariably be 
appended where there is delay in laying of Notifications. 
The Committee, in the absence of delay statements, are 
not able to know the reasons behind the delay in laying of 
these Notifications. The Committee, therefore, impresses 
upon the Ministry to strictly adhere to the Committee’s 
recommendations  that in case there is  any delay in 
laying, a delay statement should invariably be appended 
so that the valid reasons for such delay are brought to its 
notice of the Committee.  
(ii) Ministry of Coal 
 
The Ministry of Coal have laid only one Notification 
(Sl. No. 19) which was delayed by 7 months and, moreover, 
Ministry did not even bother to append a delay statement 
citing the reasons for such delay on their part. 
 
 The Committee notes that the only Notification 
that Ministry of Coal have laid, has been delayed by seven 
months. Further, there is no reason given for this delay.  
This is in contravention of Committee’s recommendation 
given in its 135th Report that Notifications which are 
delayed should invariably be accompanied by a delay 
statement. The Committee would like the Ministry of Coal 
to take necessary steps to obviate such delays and, in case 
of delay in laying of Notifications, a delay statement 
should invariably be accompanied with them. 
 
(iii) Ministry of Communications and Information 
Technology 

 (Department of Telecommunications) 
 
 The Ministry of Communications and Information 
Technology  (Department of Telecommunications)  have laid 
11 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 31 to 41). Two of them (Sl. Nos. 31 
& 32) have been delayed by 5 months each and are 
accompanied with delay statement. The reason given by the 
Ministry for delay is as under:- 
  
"The TRAI Regulation No. 5/2018 - 
Telecommunications Consumers Education 
and Protection Fund (Fourth Amendment) 
Regulations, 2018, dated 18.07.2018  and 
TRAI Regulation No. 6/2018 - The Telecom 
Commercial Communications Customer 
Preference Regulations, 2018, dated 
19.07.2018 could not be laid down in 
Monsoon Session, 2018 due to some 
unavoidable administrative delay." 
 
 The Committee is not satisfied with the reasons  
'unavoidable' stated for delay by the Ministry of 
Communications and Information Technology  
(Department of Telecommunications) and recommends 
that more elaborate statement giving reasons for delay 
needs to be appended with the notification. To obviate 
such instances of delay in laying of subordinate legislation 
in future, the Ministry should take necessary steps, 
administrative or otherwise, to address the issues causing 
delay. 
 
(iv) Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public 
Distribution 
 (Department of Consumer Affairs) 

 
 The Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public 
Distribution (Department of Consumer Affairs) have laid 8 
Notifications (Sl. Nos. 42 – 49) and one of these (Sl. No. 49) 
has been delayed by 9 months. There is no delay statement 
appended to the Notification. 
  
The Committee notes with concern the delay in 
laying of one of the Notification of the Ministry of 
Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution 
(Department of Consumer Affairs) on the Table of the 
House. The Committee notes that  the Ministry had not 
communicated the circumstances causing delay in laying 
of the Notification as no delay statement has been 
attached thereto. The Committee, therefore, advises the 
Ministry  to strictly adhere to the time schedule in future 
in laying of the Notifications and append a delay 
statement where there is delay in laying of Notification on 
the Table of the Council.  
 
(v) Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate 
Change 
 
 The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate 
Change have laid 9 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 96 to 104).  Out of 
these, 2 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 96 & 97) have been delayed 
by  4 months each and no delay statement appended  to any of 
them. 
 
 The Committee is constrained to note that there 
has been delay in  laying of the two Notifications by the 
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change. 
Moreover, there is no delay statement appended to throw 
light on the factors which caused this delay. Further, the 

Committee desires that delay statements should 
invariably be appended where there is delay in laying of 
Notifications. The Committee, therefore, impresses upon 
the Ministry to strictly adhere to the time schedule as 
prescribed in Committee’s 131st Report and,  in case of 
any delay in laying, a delay statement needs to be 
appended. 
 
(vi) Ministry of Finance 
 (a)  (Department of Economic Affairs) 
 
 The Ministry of Finance (Department of Economic 
Affairs) have laid 47 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 105 to 151).  Out 
of these, 2 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 111 & 112) have been  
delayed by 8 months and 5 months respectively and no delay 
statement, were appended to any of these delayed 
Notifications.  
 
 The Committee notes that out of 47 Notifications 
laid by the Ministry of  Finance (Department of Economic 
Affairs) two Notifications were delayed and delay 
statements were not attached. The Committee would like 
to impress upon the Ministry of Finance (Department of 
Economic Affairs) that it is obligatory on the part of the 
Ministry to communicate the circumstances causing delay 
in laying of Notifications and also to append delay 
statement thereto. The Committee would, therefore, 
advise the  Ministry  to strictly adhere to the time 
schedule in laying of the Notifications and if there is delay 
then to append a delay statement. 
 
(b)  (Department of Financial Services) 
 

 The Ministry of Finance (Department of Financial 
Services) have laid 16 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 152 to 167), out 
of which, 7 Notifications have been delayed.  Out of 7 
delayed Notifications,  6  Notifications (Sl. Nos. 152 to 156 & 
164) had no delay statement appended to them, while delay 
statement had been attached to one notification (Sl. No. 160). 
The reasons forwarded by the Ministry for delay is as under:- 
 “The Notification dated 17.2.2018 regarding amendment 
in Corporation Bank Officers' Service Regulations, 1982, 
published in the Gazette of India, vide No. 15 on 14.4.2018 - 
20.4.2018. 
 As the Bank did not furnish the requisite copies of 
Gazette Notification within the stipulated period, clarification 
was sought from Corporation Bank. 
 The bank has reported that due to communication gap 
from the Publication Department with the bank, requisite 
copies of Gazette Notification regarding amendment in 
Officers' Service Regulations could not be forwarded for 
laying within stipulated time. It has further expressed regret 
for inadvertent omission. 
 In view of the above, the said Notification could not be 
laid on the Table of the both the Houses on earlier occasions. 
Delay in this regard is deeply regretted and may please be 
condoned." 
 
 The Committee notes the time taken by the 
Ministry of Finance (Department of Financial Services) in 
laying of their Notifications, which ranges from seven 
months to twenty months.  The Committee is unable to 

accept the reasons given by the Ministry of Finance 
(Department of Financial Services) for the delay in laying 
due to communication gap from the Publication 
Department with the bank, and that requisite copies of 
Gazette Notification regarding amendment in Officers' 
Service Regulations could not be forwarded for laying 
within the stipulated time. Further, the Committee is 
astounded by the fact that the remaining 6 Notifications 
had no delay statements attached thereto. It only reflects 
the lack of seriousness in the part of the Ministry in 
fulfilling its constitutional responsibility towards the 
Parliament. The Committee directs the Ministry to be 
careful about laying of its Subordinate Legislation in time. 
 
 
(c) (Department of Revenue) 
 
 The Ministry of Finance (Department Revenue) have 
laid 151 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 168 – 318). Out of these, 4 
Notifications (Sl. Nos. 214, 215, 217 and 218) have been  
delayed with delay periods ranging from  5 months to 7 
months and no delay statement has been attached  to any of 
the notifications so delayed. 
 
 The Committee takes a serious view not only for 
the delay in laying of the four Notifications  on the Table 
of the Council,  but also for its failure to append the 
required delay statement thereto. The 
Ministry/Department must realise the possible 
implications of failing to meet this requirement that 
tantamounts to diluting Executive’s accountability to the 
Parliament. It must, therefore,  ensure to lay the 
Notifications well within the time frame and if there is a 

delay, it must append a delay statement in all cases in 
future. 
 
 (vii) Ministry of Health and Family Welfare 
 (Department of Health and Family Welfare) 
 
 The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare 
(Department of Health and Family Welfare) have laid 22 
Notifications (Sl. Nos. 323 - 344), out of  these 9 
Notifications  (Sl. Nos. 323 to 329 and 335 & 336) have been 
delayed. The delay period ranges from 8 months to 11 months 
and no delay statement has been attached to any of these 
delayed Notifications. 
 
The Committee finds it astounding that 40.9% (9 
out of 22) Notifications laid by the Ministry were delayed 
and none of these notifications have any delay statements 
attached to them. While there may be a reason for the 
delay, there cannot be any reason for not furnishing the 
statement therefor. The Ministry of Health and Family 
Welfare (Department of Health and Family Welfare) must 
understand the implications for not doing so regularly 
and that too in such a large number of cases. The 
Committee finds this callous approach of the  Ministry 
unacceptable and directs that in future, it should avoid 
delay and if it happens, then invariably append a delay 
statement. 
 
 (viii) Ministry of Home Affairs 
  
The Ministry of Home Affairs have laid 33 
Notifications (Sl. Nos. 345 –377). Out of  these,  13 
Notifications  have been delayed. Whereas 12 Notifications 
(Sl. Nos. 345, 347 to  351, 365 to 359  & 370) have been 

delayed for periods ranging from of 5 months to 7 months and 
are not accompanied with delay statement. However,  one 
Notification (Sl. No. 372) has been delayed by 5 months and 
a delay statement has been appended to it. The reasons of 
delay given by the Ministry is as under:- 
 
“As per Section 155 of  sub-section (2) of the 
Sashastra Seema Bal Act, 2007 (53 of 2007), the Recruitment 
Rules for the posts of Head Constable (Electrician), Constable 
(Mason), Constable (Carpenter), Constable (Plumber), 
Constable (Black Smith) and Constable (Painter) namely 
Sashastra Seema Bal (Combatised) Engineering Cadre Group 
'C' posts Recruitment Rules, 2018 notified vide GSR 220 
dated 17.07.2018, under sub-section (3) of Section 155 of 
SSB Act, 2007, were required to be laid before the House of 
Parliament while it is in Session for a total period of 30 days 
soon after these were made. The hard copy of the notification 
was downloaded from web-site (E-gazette) of the 
Government of India Press on 02.08.2018. The Recruitment 
Rules, however could not be laid on the Table of Rajya Sabha 
during the previous Monsoon Session, 2018 before closure of 
the Session due to the fact that by the time of its submission 
on 07.08.2018 the laying schedule was already over. 
 
2. Accordingly, Recruitment Rules are now being laid 
down on the Table of Rajya Sabha in the current Session.” 
 
The reasons cited by Ministry of Home Affairs,  i.e. 
'Notification could not be laid on the Table because the 
copies of Notification was downloaded from web-site (E-
gazette) of the Government of India Press on 02.08.2018  
during the previous Monsoon Session, 2018 before closure 
of the Session due to the fact that by the time of its 
submission on 07.08.2018 the laying schedule was already 

over,'  is not a convincing reason. Further, no effort has 
been made to lay it on the Table of the Council during the 
247th and 248th Session. However, the more serious  issue 
is that 13 Notifications were delayed and no delay 
statements were appended in case of 12 of these delayed 
Notifications. It is obligatory on the part the Ministry to 
lay the notification within the prescribed time schedule. 
The Committee, therefore, impresses upon  the Ministry 
to  devise suitable mechanism to avoid such instances of 
delay in future, particularly, on account of delay in getting 
printed copies of Notifications from Printing Press so as to 
adhere to the time schedule as prescribed in Committee’s 
131st Report. 
 
(ix) Ministry of  Housing  and Urban Affairs 
 
The Ministry of Housing  and Urban Affairs have laid 
5 Notifications (Sl.Nos. 378 - 382), out of these only one 
Notification (Sl.No.382) has been delayed and that too by 8 
months and is accompanied by a  delay statement. The reason 
given by the Ministry for delay is as under:- 
 
 "In accordance with Section 86 (1) of the Real Estate 
(Regulation and Development) Act, 2016, every rule made by 
the Central Government, every regulation made by the 
Authority under the Union Territory of Delhi and the Union 
Territories without Legislature and every notification issued 
by the Central Government under this Act, shall be laid, as 
soon as may be after it is made before each House of 
Parliament, while it is in session, for a total period of thirty 
days which may be comprised in one session or in two or 
more successive sessions, and if, before the expiry of the 
session immediately following the session or the successive 
sessions aforesaid, both Houses agree in making any 

modification in the rule of regulation or in the notification, as 
the case may be, or both Houses agree that the rule or 
regulation or the notification should not be made, the rule or 
regulation or notification, as the case may be shall thereafter 
have effect only in such modified form or be of no effect, as 
the case may be, so however, that any such modification or 
annulment shall be without prejudice to the validity of 
anything previously done under that rule or regulation or 
notification, as the case may be. 
 As per above provision, the above mentioned 
Notification was to be laid in both the Houses of Parliament 
during the Budget Session of 2017, but it got delayed 
inadvertently." 
 
The Committee notes the reason given by the 
Ministry of Housing  and Urban Affairs that caused delay 
in laying of the Notifications and finds it very cryptic as 
no specific reason for the delay has been furnished. The 
Committee, though, appreciates that a delay statements 
has been attached. But the Committee, feels that tabling of 
Gazette Notification is of utmost public importance and it 
is prime responsibility of the Ministry to discharge its 
duty to Parliament and getting it delayed inadvertently is 
inexcusable. 
   
 
(x) Ministry of Labour and Employment 
 
 The Ministry of Labour and Employment  have laid 5 
Notifications (Sl. Nos. 406 – 410). Only 1 Notification (Sl. 
No. 406) has been delayed by 9 months and there is no delay 
statement appended to it.  
  

  The Committee notes that though there has been 
delay in laying of one Notification of the Ministry, but  no 
delay statement has been attached to it. The Committee 
expects the Ministry to be careful and responsible in these 
matters henceforth.  The Ministry of Labour and 
Employment should ensure such compliance in future 
with due caution so that such recurrence does’nt take 
place. 
 
 
(xi) Ministry of Law and Justice  
 (Department of Legal Affairs) 
  
The Ministry of Law and Justice (Department of 
Legal Affairs) have laid 5 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 411 – 415). 
Out  of these, 4 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 411 to 414) have  been 
delayed. The delay period ranges from 5 months to 8 months 
and no delay statement have been attached to any of these 
delayed Notifications.  
 
The Committee is astounded by the fact that  the 
Ministry of Law and Justice (Department of Legal 
Affairs) did not  lay its papers on the Table of the Council 
in time. The Committee expects a lot from this Ministry 
and being the custodian of Law and Justice of the country, 
it is their primal duty  to follow the established law and 
moreso to lead by example. Further, the Ministry of  Law 
and Justice did not append any delay statement to these 
delayed notifications. The Committee finds this 
unacceptable. In all the delayed cases, the delays ranges 
from 5 months to 8 months, and the Ministry has not 
taken any responsibility to inform the Council of the 
reasons for the delays. The Committee, therefore, 
recommends that appropriate steps may be taken to 

obviate any such delay in future for laying of Notifications 
on the Table of the  House by the Ministry of Law and 
Justice (Department of Legal Affairs) and in case of 
delays, a delay statement should invariably be appended 
thereto. 
 
 
(xii) Ministry of Power 
 
The Ministry of Power have laid 10 Notifications (Sl. 
Nos. 424  – 433). Out of  these,  8  Notifications  have been 
delayed. Whereas 6 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 424  to  429) have 
been delayed by long periods ranging from  2 years and 4 
months to 3 years and 5 months, these were accompanied by 
delay statements. However,  2 Notifications  (Sl. Nos. 430  
and 431) has been delayed by 11 months and one year 
respectively and no delay statement has been appended to 
them. The reasons of delay given by the Ministry is as under:- 
 
(i)  "The Bureau of Energy Efficiency (Particulars 
and Manner of   their Display on Labels of 
Stationary Storage Type Electric   Water Heater) 
Regulations, 2016 - published in the Gazette of  
 India, Extraordinary, Part-III-Section 4 dated 7th 
 September,   2016. 
(ii) The Bureau of Energy Efficiency (Particulars 
and Manner of   their Display on Labels of 
Colour Televisions) Regulations,   2016 - published 
in the Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part-III   - 
Section 4 dated 26th May, 2016. 
(iii) The Bureau of Energy Efficiency (Particulars 
and Manner of   their Display on Labels of 
Household Direct Cool    
 Refrigerators) Regulation, 2016 - published in the 

Gazette of   India, Extraordinary, Part-III - Section 
4 dated 26th May, 2016. 
(iv) Energy Conservation (Energy Consumption 
Norms and  Standards for Designated Consumers, Form, 
Time Within  which, and Manner of Preparation and 
Implementation of  Scheme, Procedure for issue of Energy 
Savings Certificate and  Value of Per metric Ton of Oil 
equivalent of Energy  Consumed) Amendment Rules, 2016 - 
published in the Gazette  of India, Extraordinary, Part-II - 
Section 3, sub-section (i)  dated  31st  March, 2016. 
(v) Energy Conservation (Energy Consumption 
Norms, Form,  Time within which and Manner of Preparation 
and  implementation of Scheme, Procedure for 
Issue of Energy  Savings Certificate and Value of Per 
Metric Ton of Oil  Equivalent of Energy Consumed) 
Amendment Rules, 2015 -  published in the Gazette  of 
India, Extraordinary, Part-II -  Section 3, sub-section 
(i)  dated 30th June, 2015.

Submission of  Report on the Status of Energy

Amendment Rules, 2015 - published in the Gazette  of India,

 19 th November, 2015.

been published/notified in the Gazette of India Extraordinary 
in exercise of the powers conferred under Section 58 of the 
Energy Conservation Act, 2001. Similarly, the above said

2. Under the provisions contained in the sub-section (1) 
of the section 59 of the EC Act, 2001, every rule/regulation 
made by the Central Government and every regulation made 
under this Act shall be laid, as soon as may be after it is 
made, before each House of Parliament. 
 
3. It is submitted that the files of the respective 
notifications were inadvertently sent for recording without 
completing the requirement of laying them in the Parliament. 
 
4. It is requested to kindly condone the delay in laying 
the above notifications." 
  
 The Notifications could not be laid on time due to 
inadvertence and the notifications were sent for recording 
without completing the requirement of laying them in the 
Parliament, is not acceptable to the Committee. The 
Committee wonders as to how it has taken such a  long 
period of time ranging from 2 years and 4 months to 3 
years and 5 months for the Ministry to realize their 
mistake. It only reflects the lack of seriousness on the part 
of the Ministry in fulfilling its responsibility to Parliament 
on one hand and also to deny the rights of Members to 
analyses/study such Notification and move motion for 
modification/annulment etc. The Ministry should find 
some suitable mechanism to eliminate such instances of 
delays in future. The Committee expects the Ministry to 
be more careful about laying of its papers and see that 
persons responsible for this are held accountable so that 
there are no such recurrences. 
 
(xiii) Ministry of Road Transport and Highways 
 

 The Ministry of Road Transport and  Highways have 
laid 67 Notifications on the Table of the House (Sl. Nos. 441 
– 507).  A total of 9 Notifications have been delayed out of 
which 7 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 491 to 497) are accompanied 
by delay statements and 2 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 441 & 442) 
have no delay statements appended with them. The delay 
period ranges from 5 months to 11 months. The reasons given 
by the Ministry is that it took some time to complete the 
procedural formalities and, therefore, papers could not be laid 
in time.. 
 
 The reasons for delay given by the Ministry of 
Road Transport and Highways that it took some time to 
collect the papers and complete the procedural 
formalities, is not convincing. Instead, it shows the 
Ministry in very poor light and its careless attitude 
towards discharging its statutory obligation. The 
Committee wonders as to how can it take 5 months to 11  
months to receive Notifications and to complete 
procedural formalities. The Committee feels that Ministry 
did not take adequate precaution to avoid such  delays. 
The Committee further takes a serious view of the fact 
that even after delay of five months and nine months in 
certain case, Ministry did not feel it necessary to append a 
delay statement so as to apprise the Parliament  of the 
reasons for delay in laying of Notifications on the Table. 
The Committee recommends that the Ministry should put 
in place measures to avoid delay in completing the 
procedural formalities in time so that such delays are 
avoided. 
 
(xiv) Ministry of Textiles 
 

 The Ministry of Textiles have laid 2 Notifications (Sl. 
Nos. 524 & 525) on the Table of the House during the 
Session. One of them (Sl. No. 525) has been delayed by 9 
Months and has no delay statement appended thereto.  
  
 The Committee notes with concern  that Ministry 
of Textiles did not act promptly to lay the Notification (Sl. 
No. 525) on the Table of the House. Had they taken 
prompt action, the delay would not have occurred. The 
Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry of 
Textiles should act promptly to avoid such delay and in 
case of such delays in laying of Notifications, delay 
statements should invariably be accompanied with them.
  
 
 
3.   The Committee impresses upon all the 
Ministries/Departments to take immediate and concrete steps 
to ensure timely and proper laying of subordinate legislation. 
The Committee, accordingly, wishes to bring to the notice of 
all Ministries/Departments of the Government of India, 
particularly, the defaulting ones, the following 
recommendations, as contained in its 7th, 10th, 47th, 131st, 
135th , 152nd,  192nd , 201st, 212th and 213th Reports: 
 
 “The Committee desires that for the convenience of 
the public and Members, Ministries should henceforth 
send copies of 'order' duly authenticated by the Ministers 
concerned, incorporating therein all the corrections and 
amendments issued till date of laying such 'orders' instead 
of laying the uncorrected copy along with corrigenda. The 
Committee feels that to obviate any legal or technical 
difficulty, Ministries should examine whether there is any 

necessity of assigning a separate G.S.R. No. to a 
corrigendum at the time of its publication in the Gazette 
and whether such a corrigendum should not be published 
without assigning any G.S.R. No. The Committee would, 
therefore, like to impress upon all Ministries of the 
Government of India that the present practice of laying 
the rules without incorporating corrigenda in the body of 
the rules is not a healthy one. The Committee hopes that 
the Ministries will ensure supply of only corrected copies 
of the rules for laying on the Table so that they depict a 
true and correct picture and serve the desired purpose."
  
(7th  Report) 
(Presented on 12th  May, 1969) 
Formula for laying of Statutory Rules 
 
 The Committee approve the following draft revised 
formula for laying of Statutory Rules before both Houses 
of Parliament which the Ministry of Law and Justice 
propose to incorporate in all future legislation which 
provide for making of rules by the Central 
Government:— 
 
 "Every rule made by the Central Government under 
this Act shall be laid, as soon as may be after it is 
made, before each House of Parliament, while it is in 
session, for a total period of thirty days which may be 
comprised in one session or in two or more successive 
sessions, and if, before the expiry of the session 
immediately following the session or the successive 
sessions aforesaid, both Houses agree in making any 
modification in the rule or both Houses agree that the 
rule should not be made, the rule shall thereafter 
have effect only in such modified form or be of no 

effect, as the case may be; so, however that any such 
modification or annulment shall be without prejudice 
to the validity of anything previously done under that 
rule." 
  
The Committee recommend that the revised formula 
should be incorporated not only in new legislation but also 
in the existing Acts as and when Bills to amend them are 
brought before Parliament. The Ministry should also 
incorporate the new formula in the Bills pending before 
Parliament. This will, in the opinion of the Committee, 
bring about uniformity in the matter expeditiously. 
 
(10th  Report) 
(presented on 24th May, 1971) 
 
Time period for laying 
 
 “Orders required to be laid before the House should 
be laid (i) if the House is not in Session, during the Session 
immediately following the date of publication of the Order 
in the Official Gazette and (ii) if the House is in Session, 
on the date of the publication of the Order, during its 
continuance and in case the time lag between the date of 
publication and the date of the closing of the Session is less 
than 15 clear days, before the expiry of the Session 
immediately following the said Session. All the 
Ministries/Departments of Government of India should 
henceforth comply with this schedule in the matter of 
laying of the Orders issued under various Acts of 
Parliament on the Table of the Rajya Sabha. 
 
(131st Report) 

(Presented on 15th  December 2000) 
 
Assigning distinctive number to each Notification 
 
 “In the opinion of the Committee, every notification 
should be assigned a distinctive number in order to give it 
a separate identity and similarly, no notification should be 
published/laid which does not carry a notification 
number. The Committee expects all 
Ministries/Departments of Government of India to 
exercise caution in this regard. In case where there are 
more than one Notifications under a single file, the 
Ministries/Departments should ensure that the file 
number on each notification should be suitably 
distinguished from one another.” 
(152nd Report) 
(Presented on 26th  August 2004)  
 
 
Appending delay statement in case of delay 
 
 “The Committee has, time and again, emphasized 
that it is essential that in case there is a delay in the laying 
of Statutory Orders, the concerned Ministry/Department 
should invariably append a delay statement along with the 
Notifications being laid so as to apprise Parliament of the 
causes of delay. The Committee desires all 
Ministries/Departments to take a note of this, since the 
intention is that through the process of formulation of a 
delay statement, the Ministry is able to introspect, identify 
bottlenecks and devise remedial measures”. 
 
(135th Report) 

(Presented on 27th  July 2001) 
  
Time limit for rule making process 
  
“The Committee feels that the rule-making process 
could well have been completed within the time 
limit of six months which the Committee has laid 
down for making of rules under an Act after 
coming into force of that Act. ................. Where 
however, a Ministry does not find it possible to 
adhere to the time limit, they should inform the 
Committee of the reasons why they cannot make 
rules within the time limit and seek extension of 
time for completing the rule-making process.” 
(47th Report) 
(Presented on 14th  September 1981) 
 
 
 “In addition to the concern expressed by the 
Committee over delay in laying of Notifications on the 
Table of the House, the Committee also express their deep 
concern over delay in framing of rules/regulations under 
different Acts. The Committee in its 47th report presented 
to the House on 14.9.1981 has recommended that the rule-
making process should be completed within a period of six 
months of the coming into force of an Act. The Committee 
has further recommended that in case a Ministry is not 
able to adhere to this time limit, it should seek extension 
of time for completing the rule-making process. The 
recommendation of the committee reads as follows:- 
 

  “The Committee feels that the rule-
making process could well have been completed 
within the time limit of six months which the 
Committee has laid down for making of rules 
under an Act after coming into force of that Act. 
Where however, a Ministry does not find it possible 
to adhere to the time limit, they should inform the 
Committee of the reasons why they cannot make 
rules within the time limit and seek extension of 
time for completing the rule-making process.” 
  
 The Committee is constrained to take note of the 
fact that the Ministries/Departments of Government of 
India are not complying with the Committee’s 
recommendation to complete the process of framing of 
subordinate legislation contemplated under various Acts 
of Parliament within a period of six months. At the same 
time, the Committee also does not receive requests for 
extension of time for completing the rule-making process 
in terms of its recommendations as above from most of 
the Ministries/Departments. The Committee takes a 
serious note of the prevailing situation in which the 
Ministries/Departments are neither able to complete the 
task of framing rules/regulations under different Acts 
within the given six months’ period nor do they suo-motu 
approach the Committee for seeking extension of time. 
The Committee further notes that in order to ensure 
timely framing of rules/regulations it has taken an 
initiative to monitor the progress of framing of 
subordinate legislation in respect of all legislations 
brought about by different Ministries/Departments of 
Government of India from the year 2003 onwards with a 
view to ensure that the framing of subordinate legislation 

is not delayed. The Committee, however, finds that the 
responses from the Ministries/Departments have not been 
prompt in this monitoring exercise undertaken on behalf 
of the Committee. 
  
 In view of the above position, the Committee once 
again reiterates its recommendation that the 
Ministries/Departments should ensure putting in place 
subordinate legislation positively within a period of six 
months of coming into force of the Act. The Committee 
further recommends that in case the Ministry fails to meet 
with this deadline, they should invariably approach the 
Committee for seeking extension of time. The Committee 
further recommends that in cases where the time limit of 
six months is not adhered to, they should, while laying 
rules/regulations before the Parliament invariably lay a 
statement explaining the reasons why the framing of 
rules/regulations was delayed beyond six months so as to 
keep the Parliament apprised of the compliance of the 
Parliament’s mandate  conferred upon the Executive.” 
(192nd Report) 
(Presented on 26th  August 2011)  
 
 
The Committee observes that the whole process of 
enacting laws is defeated if rules are not framed and laid 
on the Table of the House in time.  A reasonable delay 
could be understood but unjustifiably long delays should 
be avoided and the Ministries should work towards 
improving this position.  The Committee hopes that 
Ministry would strive to keep the delay to the minimum 
and take care that Notifications are laid on the Table of 

the House at the first available opportunity after 
publication of Notifications. 
 
The Committee would like to impress upon the 
Ministry that it is their responsibility to ensure that copies 
of the Notifications are printed timely and for this 
purpose, they need to evolve a suitable mechanism to 
ensure that notifications are laid in time.   The Committee 
is happy that the Ministry has evolved an internal 
mechanism/ procedure for this purpose.  The Committee 
hopes that it would take action accordingly in order to 
comply with the prescribed schedule in the matter of 
laying of statutory Notifications. 
 
The Ministry must take appropriate step to remove 
lacuna, if any, administrative or otherwise, causing such 
long delay by being little proactive and prompt.  Further, 
the Ministries should take it up with the Ministry of 
Urban Development for late receiving of printed copies of 
the Notification. 
212th  Report 
(Presented on  3rd September, 2013) 
 
 
Uploading Notifications on websites 
 
  Rules/Regulations/Orders/bye-laws are laid by 
different Ministries on the Table of the House under 
various provisions of parent Acts passed by Parliament. 
These Rules/ Regulations/Orders/bye-laws are published 
in the official Gazette before being laid on the Table of the 
House. Even after they are laid, it is very difficult to get 
access to these Notifications. The Committee recommends 
that such Rules/Regulations/Orders, etc. laid on the Table 

of the House should be invariably uploaded on the 
websites of respective Ministries immediately on the same 
day when they have been laid on the Table of the House, 
for information of Members of Parliament and people at 
large for their easy access. 
 
201st Report 
(Presented on 14th December, 2012)  
 
 
Late availability of printed copies 
 
 “The Committee is not inclined to accept the late 
availability of printed copies of Notifications from the 
Government of India Press as the reason for delay in 
laying of the Notifications. The Committee directs all the 
Ministries that in case there is a delay in procuring 
printed copies in time, they may obtain G.S.R. and S.O. 
numbers from the Government of India Press and 
prepare requisite number of copies in cyclostyled form for 
laying in the Parliament. The Committee also 
recommends that this process may be adopted by 
Ministries suo moto on immediate basis so as to avoid such 
delays henceforth”. 
213th  Report 
(Presented on  19th February, 2014)

Members and the following items were taken up for 
discussion. 

 239th and 240th Report on Statutory Orders laid on 
the Table of the Rajya Sabha, during its 250th 
session. 
 
3. The Committee during the course of it discussion 
on the 239th and 240th Reports took note of the delay in 
laying of rules/regulations under different Acts. The 
Committee was of the opinion that the 
Ministries/Departments should strictly follow the 
recommendations of the Committee regarding the laying 
of rules/regulations under different Acts as contained in 
131st Report of the Committee. The Committee thereupon 
decided to recommend that in cases where the prescribed 
time limit for laying of Subordinate Legislation is not 
adhered to by the Ministries/Departments, they should, 
while laying the rules/regulations before the Parliament, 
also lay a statement explaining the reasons for the said 
delay so as to keep the Parliament apprised of the reasons 
for the delay. 
4. Thereafter, the Committee adopted the reports 
unanimously. The Committee authorized the Chairman 
and in his absence Shri V. Vijayasai Reddy and Shri 

Amar Patnaik to present the reports to the House on the 
12th December, 2019.

REPORT           
 
 CHAPTER I 
      INTRODUCTION 
 
1. BACKGROUND 
 
 Rule 204 of the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in 
the Council of States (Rajya Sabha) provides that there shall be a 
Committee on Subordinate Legislation to scrutinize and report to the 
Council whether the powers to make rules, regulations, bye-laws, 
schemes or other statutory instruments conferred by the Constitution 
or delegated by Parliament have been properly exercised within such 
conferment or delegation, as the case may be.  
1.2. Mandate  
 Legislations passed by the Parliament and subsequently 
enacted after being assented to by the President of India, are 
implemented by the Executive i.e., various Ministries/Departments of 
Government of India. It is a well recognized principle that the laws 
enacted by Parliament cannot be exhaustive enough to visualize each 
and every situation that may arise during the course of its 

implementation and to make provisions for it in the Act in 
anticipation. The Central Acts, therefore, if necessary,  contain a 
provision authorizing the Government to frame detailed 
rules/regulations, etc. to enable it to implement the provisions of the 
Act. These rules/regulations framed in exercise of the powers 
conferred by an Act of Parliament are termed as “Subordinate 
Legislation”.  
Rule 209 of the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in 
the Council of States lays down that after each rule, regulation, bye-
law, scheme or other statutory instrument framed in pursuance of the 
Constitution/Act or the legislative functions delegated by the 
Parliament to a subordinate authority and which is required to be laid 
before Parliament, is so laid before the Council, the Committee shall, 
in particular consider: 
  
(i)  Whether the Order is in accord with the provisions of the 
Constitution/Act pursuant to which it is made;  
(ii)  Whether the Order contains matter which, in the opinion of 
the Committee, should more properly be dealt within an Act 
of Parliament;  
(iii) Whether the Order contains imposition of taxation;  
(iv)  Whether the Order directly or indirectly bars the jurisdiction 
of the Courts; 
 
(iv) 
 
 (v)  Whether the Order gives retrospective effect to any of the 
provisions in respect of which the Constitution or the Act 
does not expressly give any such power;  
(vi) Whether the Order involves expenditure from the 
Consolidated Fund of India or the public revenues;  
(vii) Whether the Order appears to make some unusual or 
unexpected use of the powers conferred by the Constitution 
or the Act pursuant to which it is made;  

(viii) Whether there appears to have been unjustifiable delay in its 
publication or laying before Parliament; and 
(ix) Whether for any reason, the form or purport of the order calls 
for any elucidation.  
 
1.3 Statutory Requirement for laying  
 
 The Committee on Subordinate Legislation, Rajya Sabha had, 
in its 10th Report presented to the House on the 24th May, 1971, inter-
alia recommended a standard laying formula to be incorporated not 
only in new legislation but also in existing Acts as and when Bills to 
amend them are brought before Parliament:- 
 “Every rule made by the Central Government under this Act 
shall be laid, as soon as may be after it is made, before each 
House of Parliament, while it is in session, for a total period of 
thirty days which may be comprised in one session or in two or 
more successive sessions, and if, before the expiry of the 
session immediately following the session or the successive 
sessions aforesaid,  both Houses  agree in  making any 
modification in  the rule  or both Houses agree that the rule 
should not be made, the rule shall thereafter have effect only in 
such modified form or be of no effect, as the case may be; so, 
however that any such modification or annulment shall be 
without prejudice to the validity of anything previously done 
under that rule.” 
 
Now, all statutes contain the above cited provision for making 
rules/regulations and for laying the same before both Houses of 
Parliament.   
      
1.4 Time limit for laying of rules/regulations 
 
 As per the recommendations contained in para 33 of the 1st 
Report of the Committee, all the Orders including rules etc., are 
required to be laid on the Table of the House: - 

(a)  within a period of 15 days after their publication in the 
Gazette, if the House is in session; and 
(b)  if the House is not in session, within a period of 15 days 
after the commencement  of  the  next  session. 
(V) 
 However, in case of notifications relating to a state under the 
President’s rule, due to difficulties faced by certain Ministry, the 
Committee vide its recommendations contained in its 6th Report (para 
17-19) relaxed this time period to 30 days from the date of publication 
of the rules, orders, notifications etc., in the State Gazette. 
 
1.5 Motion for annulment or modification of rules/regulations 
laid on the Table of the House 
 
 As per recommendations of the Committee contained in its 10th 
Report (cited at para 1.3 ante), after the rules/regulations are laid on 
the Table of the House, Members can move motion for modification or 
annulment of the rules/regulations. The statutory period of laying of 30 
days might be completed in one session or two or more successive 
sessions. Further, states the recommendation of the Committee 
contained in its 75th Report (Para 2.5), as reproduced below:- 
 
"The Committee agrees with the view of the Committee on 
Subordinate Legislation Lok Sabha (Seventh Lok Sabha) expressed 
in its 20th Report, that laying on the Table of all Orders' in 
pursuance of powers delegated by Parliament is very significant, 
as it affords an opportunity to Members of Parliament if they so 
desire to move any amendment or modification to such 'order'; 
including a Motion for their annulment.”  
 Hence, a reading of both these recommendations together 
indicates that Members have a right to suggest/move motion for 
annulment/modifications in the 'Order' for a time period till one 
additional session immediately following the session in which the 
period of 30 days is completed. If the modification or annulment is 

carried by the Houses of Parliament, the rules/regulations stand 
annulled or modified to the extent agreed to by the Houses of 
Parliament. 
 
1.6 Role of the Committee on Subordinate Legislation, Rajya 
Sabha with regard to unjustifiable delay in laying 
 
 One of the important function of the Committee, according to 
Rule 209(viii), is to see whether there has been unjustifiable delay in 
the publication or laying of the rules/regulations before the Parliament. 
The Committee monitors the laying of the rules/regulations etc. on the 
table of Rajya Sabha during its Session through its Reports. This 
practice started with the 131st Report of the Committee on Statutory 
Orders laid on the Table of the Rajya Sabha during its 190th Session, 
presented to the House on 15th December, 2000. During the meeting of 
the Committee held on 11th December, 2000, to adopt the said report, 
the Committee decided that henceforth, it will   
  (vi) 

regularly scrutinize the notifications laid on the Table of Rajya Sabha 
from time to time and present a report to the Council in respect of each 
Session. This practice has continued since then and the present report 
is in pursuance of the said decision of the Committee.

CHAPTER II 
 
 
2.   LAYING OF STATUTORY ORDERS ON THE TABLE 
    OF RAJYA SABHA 
   
2.1 During the 248th   Session of the Rajya Sabha,     (31st January, 
2019  – 13th  February, 2019), 233 (Two Hundred Thirty-Three) 
Statutory Orders/Notifications relating to 
Rules/Regulations/Schemes/Bye-laws etc. framed under the 
Constitution/ Acts of Parliament were laid on the Table of the House 
by various Ministries/Departments of the Government of India. The 
details of the Gazette Notifications in which these were published and 
the date of their laying on the Table of the Rajya Sabha have been 
indicated Ministry-wise, in a Statement placed at Annexure.
